translations.text: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Listen, heavens, and pay attention, earth, for the Lord has spoken: “I raised children and brought them up, but they rebelled against me.”
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's feeding trough, but Israel does not know, and my people do not understand.
Woe to the sinful people, a people burdened with wrongdoing, an evil offspring, corrupt children! You have abandoned the Lord, provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger, and turned backward.
Why should you be struck again and receive still more punishment? Every head is in pain, and every heart is sick.
From the sole of the foot to the head, there is no sound place in it—only wounds, bruises, and swollen sores, neither dressed nor bandaged nor softened with oil.
Your land is devastated, and your towns are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your land before your eyes, and it lies desolate, as though overthrown by foreigners.
Daughter Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
If the Lord of hosts had not left us a remnant, we would have become like Sodom and resembled Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom! Pay attention to the law of our God, people of Gomorrah!
“What use to me are your many sacrifices?” says the Lord. “I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened animals. I do not desire the blood of bulls, lambs, or young goats.”
When you come to see my face, who has required this from your hands—that you trample my courts?
“Do not continue bringing me worthless offerings. Incense is detestable to me. At the new moons and on the Sabbath you gather an assembly; I cannot endure sweat and confinement.”
My soul hates your new moons and your festivals. They have become a burden to me; I am tired of carrying them.
“When you spread out your hands, I will turn my eyes away from you. Even if you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are full of blood.”
Wash yourselves and become clean. Remove your evil deeds from before my eyes. Stop doing evil.
Learn to do good. Seek justice and do good to the oppressed. Defend the rights of orphans and plead the cases of widows.
“Come, let us speak with one another,” says the Lord. “Even if your sins are like scarlet, they will become white as snow; even if they are red as crimson, they will become like wool.”
If you are willing and obey me, you will eat the good things of the land.
But if you are unwilling and resist, you will be devoured by the sword, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.
How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice, and righteousness lived in her, but now murderers do.
Your silver has been rejected; your tavern keepers mix in water.
Your rulers are rebellious and partners of thieves. They all love bribes and hurry to repay favors. They do not give justice to orphans, and widows’ cases never come before them.
Therefore this is what the Lord of lords, the mighty one, the strong one of Israel, says: “Woe! I will exact repayment from those who hate me and take vengeance on my enemies.”
I will turn my hand against you and refine your rebels to purity. I will remove all your evildoers.
“I will establish your judges as in former times and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you will be called the city of righteousness and the city of faithfulness.”
Zion will be redeemed through justice, and her captives through righteousness.
Wrongdoers and sinners will be broken together, and those who have abandoned the Lord will perish.
For they will be ashamed of the idols they desired and embarrassed by the gardens they chose.
For they will become like a terebinth whose leaves have fallen, and like a garden that has no water.
Their strength will become tinder, and their makers will become sparks. Both will burn together, with no one to put out the fire.
The message that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
In the last days, the mountain of the Lord’s house will be established at the head of the mountains and raised above the hills, and all nations will stream to it.

Many peoples will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For the law will go out from Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

He will judge between the nations and correct many distant peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not take up the sword against nation, and they will no longer learn warfare.
House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord.
For you have abandoned your people, the house of Jacob, because they have become full as in former times. They practice divination like the Philistines and have raised many foreign children.
Their land is filled with silver and gold, and there is no end to their treasures. Their land is filled with horses, and there is no end to their chariots.
Their land is filled with idols. They bow down to the work of their own hands, to what their fingers have made.
People have bowed down, and men have lowered themselves. Do not forgive them.
Enter the rocks and hide in the dust from the terror of the Lord and from the splendor of his might.
He will lower people’s haughty eyes, and human pride will be humbled. The Lord alone will prevail on that day.
For the day of the Lord is against everyone who is proud and exalted, and against everyone who is lifted up, to bring them low;
against all the cedars of Lebanon, tall and lofty, and against all the oaks of Bashan;
against all the high mountains and against all the lofty hills;
And against every high tower and every strong wall.
against all the ships of Tarshish and against all the splendid watchtowers.
Human pride will be humbled, and human arrogance brought low. The Lord alone will be supreme on that day.
The idols will disappear completely.
They will enter caves in the rock and holes in the ground, away from the terror of the Lord and the splendor of his might, when he rises to subdue the earth.
On that day people will throw their idols of gold and silver, which they made for themselves to worship, into emptiness and to the bats,
to enter caves in the crags and clefts in the rock, away from the terror of the Lord and the splendor of his might, when he rises to subdue the earth.
Stop relying on human beings, whose breath is in their nostrils. For what are they worth?
For look, the Lord of lords is removing from Jerusalem and Judah support and sustenance, everyone who depends on bread and everyone who depends on water.
the mighty man and the warrior, the judge and the prophet, the diviner and the elder,
the commander of fifty, the distinguished man, the counselor, the skilled carpenter, and the one who understands counsel.
I will appoint youths as their rulers, and mockers will rule over them.
The people will fall upon one another, each against his neighbor. The young will defy the old, and the despised will defy the honored.
For a man will seize his brother from his father's household and say to him, “You have clothes. Be our ruler, and let this ruin be under your authority.”
He will answer that day and say, “I will not be a leader, for there is neither bread nor clothing in my house. Do not make me ruler over the people.”
For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, because their tongues and the work of their hands have provoked the Lord and the cloud of his glory.
Their favoritism testifies against them. They have displayed their sins like Sodom and have not concealed them. Woe to them, for they have brought terrible destruction upon themselves!
Tell the righteous that it is good, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.
Woe to the wicked, evil man, for he will be repaid for the work of his hands!
The rulers of my people devour them, and women rule over them. My people, those who flatter you have led you astray and confused the course of your paths.
The Lord rises to judge; he stands to judge his people.
The Lord will enter into judgment with the elders of his people and their leaders: “You have burned the vineyard, and what you have plundered from the poor is in your houses.”
Why have you harmed my people and put the poor to shame?” says the mighty Lord.
Because the daughters of Zion have become proud and walk with their necks held high, glancing with their eyes as they go, stamping their feet and stirring up excitement.
the Lord will bring low the heads of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will expose their bodies.
On that day the Lord will remove the splendor of their clothes, their ornaments, and their braids,
their hairbands and their locks of hair,
their sidelocks, their facial ornaments, their earrings, their necklaces, and their collars,
their clasps and their bracelets,
their tunics, their outer robes, their fine linen, and their purple garments,
their clothes, their blue garments, their scarlet garments, and their entire array of finery.

There will be dust instead of their sweet fragrance. Instead of belts around their waists, they will tie on wraps; instead of locks of hair, there will be bald patches. Instead of their fine garments, they will cover themselves with sackcloth, because their beauty will be ruined.
Your strong men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle.
Her gates will lament and sit in mourning, and her victory will fall to the ground.
Seven women will seize one man on that day and say to him, “We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes. Only let us be called by your name, and take away our disgrace.”
On that day the dawning of the Lord will bring glory and honor, and the fruit of the land will bring pride and glory to those who remain of Israel.
Whoever remains in Zion and whoever is left in Jerusalem will be called holy—everyone recorded for life in Jerusalem.
The Lord will wash away the filth of the daughters of Zion and remove the blood from within Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a burning spirit.

The Lord will create over the whole established site of Mount Zion, over its surrounding areas, a cloud by day, and smoke and the brightness of a flaming fire by night, for there will be shade over all the glory.
There will be a shelter to give shade from the heat by day, and to provide cover and refuge from downpours and rain.
I will sing for my beloved my beloved’s song about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a hill in fertile country.
He cultivated it, surrounded it with a fence, and planted it with vines. He built a tower within it and also made a winepress in it. He waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced carobs.
Now, men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, judge between me and my vineyard.
What more should have been done for my vineyard that I have not done for it? Why, when I waited for it to produce grapes, did it produce carobs?
Now I will tell you what I am going to do to my vineyard: I will tear down its tower, and it will be plundered. I will break down its fence, and it will be trampled.
I will make it a wasteland. It will not be pruned or cultivated, and thorns and brushwood will grow in it. I will command the clouds not to send rain down upon it.
For the vineyard of the Lord Almighty is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are a new and beloved planting. I looked for justice, but there was plunder; for righteousness, but look—an outcry!
Woe to those who join house to house and merge field with field, so that you take possession of the land and live alone in it!
The Lord Almighty declared in my hearing: “Many houses will become ruins, with no one living in them.”
For ten acres of vineyard will produce one jar, and a homer of seed will produce one seah.
Woe to those who rise early in the morning and run after strong drink, who linger into the evening while wine sets them ablaze!
With lyres and harps, they drink wine by half-measures and quarter-measures, but they pay no attention to God's deeds and do not consider the work of his hands.
Therefore my people have gone into captivity for lack of knowledge. Their dead have multiplied from hunger, and they have suffered severely from thirst.
Therefore Sheol has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth without limit. The celebrated, the honored, and the mighty will descend into it.
Humanity will be humbled, people will be brought low, and haughty eyes will be humbled.
The Lord Almighty will be exalted through judgment, and the holy God will show himself holy through righteousness.
Lambs will graze as is their right, and inhabitants will feed on the ruins of what was built.
Woe to those who stretch out their sins like a long rope, and their sin like a cart rope!
They say, “Let the Lord hurry his deeds along quickly, so that we may see them! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, so that we may know it!”
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who make light into darkness and darkness into light, and who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and intelligent in their own estimation!
Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine, and to the mighty men who mix strong drink!
They acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of their rights.

Therefore, just as stubble is consumed by a tongue of fire that catches from a flame let loose, so they will be consumed. Their root will become like sand, and their shoots will rise like chaff, because they have rejected the law of the Lord Almighty and provoked the word of the Holy One of Israel.

Therefore the Lord's anger burned against his people. He raised his hand against them and struck them. The mountains shook, and their corpses lay like mud in the streets. Yet despite all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.
He will raise a banner for the nations far away and whistle for them from the ends of the earth, and they will come swiftly and quickly.
They will not grow weary or stumble; they will neither doze nor sleep. They will not loosen the belts around their waists, and the straps of their sandals will not break.
Their arrows are sharp and their bows fully drawn. Their horses’ hooves will be reckoned as flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind.
Their roaring is like a lion roaring, like a young lion that roars, seizes prey, and carries it away, with no one to rescue it.
On that day it will roar over them like the roaring of the sea. They will look at the land, and there will be darkness and distress, and the light will grow dark in their gloom.
In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a high throne, and the train of his robe filled his temple.
Seraphim stood above him, each with six wings. With two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
They called to one another and said, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Almighty! The whole earth is full of his glory.”
The thresholds of the doors shook at the voice of the one calling, and the house filled with smoke.
I said, “Woe to me, for I am ruined! I am a man with unclean lips, and I live among a people whose lips are unclean, yet my eyes have seen the King, the Lord Almighty.”
One of the seraphim flew to me, holding in his hand a glowing coal that he had taken from the altar with tongs.
He touched my mouth and said to me, “Look, this has touched your lips, so that your guilt may pass away and your sins may be forgiven.”
I heard the voice of the LORD saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go?” I said, “Here I am. Send me.”
He said to me, “Go and tell this people: ‘Keep listening, but do not understand; keep looking, but do not know.’

For the heart of this people has grown dull. Make their ears heavy and shut their eyes, so that they will not see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, turn back, and be forgiven.
I said, “How long, Lord?” He said, “Until the towns are ruined, without inhabitants, the houses are without people, and the land is ruined and laid waste.”
and the LORD sends the people far away, and abandonment spreads throughout the land.
Even if a tenth remains in it, it will again be burned, like a terebinth or an oak that falls from its base. The holy seed is its planting.

In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to fight against it, but they could not wage war against it.
The house of David was told, “Aram has allied itself with Ephraim.” His heart and the hearts of his people shook as the trees of the forest shake before the wind.
The Lord said to Isaiah, “Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub, beside the upper pool, on the road to the fuller’s field.”
Say to him, “Be careful and stay calm. Do not be afraid, and do not lose heart because of these two charred stumps of firebrands, because of the fierce anger of Rezin and the son of Remaliah.”
Because Aram, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah have plotted evil against you, saying,
“Let us go up against Judah, uproot it, break through it, and appoint the son of Tabeel as king over it,”
this is what the Lord GOD says: “It will not stand, and it will not happen.”’
For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered and cease to be a people.
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not believe, you will not understand either.
The Lord spoke again to Ahaz:
“Ask for a sign for yourself from the Lord your God. Ask for it deep below or high above.”
Ahaz said, “I will not ask, and I will not put the Lord my God to the test.”
He said, “Listen, house of David! Is it too little for you to weary people, that you must weary my God as well?”
Therefore the Lord God will give you a sign: Look, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and his name will be called Immanuel.
He will eat curds and honey so that he may know how to reject evil and choose good.
For before the boy knows how to reject evil and choose good, the land in which you are distressed will be abandoned by its two kings.
The Lord will bring upon you, your people, and your father’s house days unlike any that have come since the day Ephraim was separated from Judah—the king of Assyria.
On that day the Lord will whistle for the flies at the farthest reaches of the rivers of Egypt and for the bees in the land of Assyria.
They will all come and settle in the desolate valley, in the crevices of the rocks, and in all the hollows.
On that day the Lord will shave with a drunken razor from beyond the River—with the king of Assyria—the hair of the head and the hair of the feet, and he will remove the beard as well.
On that day a man will keep a young cow and two sheep alive.
Because of the abundance of milk they produce, he will eat curds, for everyone left in the land will eat honey and curds.
On that day every place where there are a thousand vines worth a thousand pieces of silver will become briars and thorns.
People will enter there with arrows and bows, because the whole land will be filled with brushwood and thorns.
All the hills where the plow used to work will be cultivated, and no fear of woodland or thorns will enter there. They will become pasture for cattle and a trampling ground for sheep.
The Lord said to me, “Take a large scroll and write on it in ordinary handwriting: ‘Hasten the captivity and hurry the plunder.’”
“Call reliable witnesses for me: Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Berechiah.”
I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. The Lord said to me, “Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz—‘Hasten the captivity, hurry the plunder.’”
For before the boy knows how to call out ‘Father’ and ‘Mother,’ the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried away before the king of Assyria.
The Lord spoke to me again:
“Because this people rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and rejoiced in Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
Therefore the Lord will bring up against them the mighty, abundant waters of the River—the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will rise above all their channels and flow over all their banks.
It will pass through Judah, sweeping over it and flooding through it, reaching up to the neck. His towering wings will fill the breadth of your land, Immanuel.
Tremble, nations, and be shattered! Listen, all you distant parts of the earth! Make yourselves strong, and be shattered!
Devise a plan, and it will be defeated. Speak a word, and it will not stand, because of Immanuel.
This is what the Lord said to me, as one holding my hand. He warned me not to walk in the way of this people, saying:
“Do not call it rebellion as this people calls it rebellion. Do not fear what they fear, and do not tremble.
Honor the mighty Lord as holy. He is the one you should fear, and he is your helper.
He will become a sanctuary, but also a stone that strikes and a rock that causes stumbling for both houses of Israel, a snare and a trap for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Many will stumble over them, fall, and be broken; they will be trapped and captured.
Bind up the testimony, and seal the law in my teaching.”
I will wait for the Lord, who has turned his face away from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him.
Here I am, with the children the Lord has given me, as a sign and a wonder in Israel from the Lord Almighty, who dwells on Mount Zion.
When they tell you, “Consult the mediums and spiritists who chirp and mutter,” those who consult the dead about the living are not God's people.
To the law and to the testimony, so that they do not speak such a word, for which no bribe can be given!
He will pass through it in hardship and hunger. When he is hungry, he will become angry and curse his king and his God, and turn upward.
He will look at the earth, and distress, darkness, anguish, and gloom will overwhelm him.

For he will not harass the distressed as in the former time, when the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali were troubled, and dominion grew strong along the sea road, beyond the Jordan River, Galilee of the nations.
The people walking in darkness have seen a great light, and light has dawned upon those living in the land of death's shadows.
You have increased the nation and enlarged its joy. They rejoice before you like those rejoicing at harvest, like those celebrating when they divide the plunder.
For you have broken the yoke of their slavery, the staff on their shoulders, and the rod of their oppressor, as on the day of Midian.
For every sound was heard amid trembling, and a garment rolled in blood became something to burn, fuel for the fire.

For a child has been born to us, and a son has been given to us. His authority rests on his shoulder, and his name has been called Wonder and Counselor, God, the Mighty One of the Ages, the Ruler of Peace.

There is no limit to the increase of his authority or to his peace upon David's throne and over his kingdom, to establish it and uphold it with justice and righteousness from now and forever. The zeal of the Lord Almighty will do this.
The Lord sent a word against Jacob, and it fell upon Israel.
All the peoples will know—Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and arrogance:
“We will lay bricks and cut hewn stones; we will cut down sycamores and replace them with cedars.”
The Lord will strengthen Rezin's oppressors against him and stir up his enemies:
Edom from the east and the Philistines from the west will devour Israel with their mouths wide open. Despite all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.
The people did not turn back even after they were struck, and they did not seek the mighty Lord.
The Lord destroyed from Israel the head and the tail, the tail and the head, in a single day.
The elder and the honored man are the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
Those who praise this people will mislead them and drown them.

Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, nor will he have compassion on their orphans and widows, because they are all godless and wicked, and every mouth speaks foolishness. Despite all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.
For sin blazes like fire. It will consume woodland and thorns and burn through the branches of the forest, and [?] will become entangled in smoke.
At the rebuke of the Lord Almighty, the earth shook, and the people became like something consumed by fire. No one will spare his brother.
He will cut off food on his right and still be hungry; he will eat on his left, but they will not be satisfied. Each man will eat the flesh of his own arm.
Manasseh against Ephraim, and Ephraim against Manasseh, and together against Judah. Despite all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.
Woe to those who issue decrees of [?] and write injustice,
To pervert justice for the poor and rob the afflicted of my people of their rights, so that they may take widows captive and plunder orphans.
What will you do on the day of reckoning, when devastation comes from far away? To whom will you flee for help, and with whom will you leave your wealth?
Unless you crouch among the prisoners, you will fall among the slain. Despite all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.
Woe to the Assyrian! He is the rod of my anger, and the staff in their hands is the instrument of my punishment.
I will send him against a godless nation and commission him against a hostile people, to take captives and seize plunder, and to trample them like mud in the streets.
But he did not imagine it this way, nor did he plan it this way in his heart. Rather, his heart is set on destroying and wiping out many nations.
For he says, “Look, my commanders are all kings.
Look, [?] is like Carchemish, Hamath like Arpad, and Samaria like Damascus.
Just as my hand reached the kingdoms of idols, whose carved images were [?] than those of Jerusalem and Samaria,
so, just as I did to Samaria and its idols, I will do to Jerusalem and its idols.”
When the Lord has completed all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the arrogant heart of the king of Assyria and the boastfulness of his haughty eyes.

For he said, “By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, because I have understanding. I have removed the boundaries of the nations, plundered their possessions, and conquered inhabited cities.
My hand found the wealth of the nations as though it were a nest. As people gather abandoned eggs, I gathered the whole earth. There was no one who raised a wing, opened his mouth, or chirped.”
Does an ax boast over the one who chops with it? Does a saw exalt itself over the one who saws with it? Or does a rod lift itself against the one who raises it?
Therefore the Lord, the mighty God, will send destruction upon his well-fed men. In place of his glory, a burning will blaze like the burning of a fire.
The light of Israel will become a fire, and his holy ones a flame. It will burn and consume his forest and his thorns in one day.
And he will consume the glory of his forest and his fruitful field, from soul to body, and it will be as though it had never existed.
The remaining trees of his forest will be so few that a child can write down their number.
On that day the remnant of Israel and those of the house of Jacob who escape will no longer rely on the one who struck them. Instead, they will truly rely on the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
A remnant will return—the remnant of Jacob—to the mighty God.
Even if your people, Israel, are like the sand in the sea, only a remnant of them will return. He has cut them off, passed sentence, and swept them away in righteousness.
For the Lord Almighty will carry out complete and decreed destruction throughout the earth.
This is what the mighty Lord says: “My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrian, who strikes you with his rod and raises his staff against you as Egypt did.
For in just a very little while, my anger and my wrath will be spent on their destruction.
The mighty Lord will stir up a whip against him, as when he struck Midian at Mount Horeb. His staff will be over the sea, and he will raise it as he did against Egypt.
On that day his oppression will pass from your shoulder and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke will be destroyed because of the anointing oils.
He came to Anath and passed through Megiddo, and at Michmash he deposited his equipment.
He crossed the pass of Geba to lodge in our house [?]. Ramah was afraid, and Gibeah of Saul fled.
Cry out aloud, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laish! Answer, Anathoth!
Madmenah has moved away, and the inhabitants of Gebim have grown strong.
This very day he stands at Nob. He has raised his hand against the mountain of the daughter of Zion and against the heights of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord, the mighty God, is forcefully overthrowing the glorious ones. Those who are tall in stature will be humbled, and those who are lofty will be brought low.
He will cut off the branches of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall in its glory.
A shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch will sprout from his root.
The Spirit of God will rest and dwell upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the Lord.
He will shine in the fear of the Lord. He will not judge according to what his eyes see or rebuke according to what his ears hear.
He will judge the poor truthfully and rebuke the evildoers of the earth fairly. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.
Righteousness will be the belt around his waist, and faithfulness the sash around his sides.
The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat. The calf, the lion cub, and the ox will graze together, and a little child will lead them.
The cow and the bear will graze together, and their young will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.
An infant will play with a viper, and a weaned child will reach his hand into an asp’s hole.
They will neither harm nor destroy anywhere on my holy mountain, because the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea.
On that day the root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the nations. The nations will seek him, and his resting place will be glorious.
On that day the Lord will again extend his hand a second time to recover the remnant of his people who remain in Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Seir, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.
He will raise a banner for the nations and gather the wandering people of Israel. He will gather the scattered people of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
Jealousy will depart from Ephraim, and Judah’s oppressors will perish. Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not oppress Ephraim.

They will plow through the flank of the Philistines along the sea, and together they will plunder the peoples of the east. They will stretch out their hands against Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will obey them.
The Lord will dry up the tongue of the sea in Egypt. He will raise his hand over the river with the force of his wind and strike it into seven streams, so that people can cross in sandals.
There will be a road for the remnant of his people who remain in Assyria, just as there was for Israel on the day they came up from the land of Egypt.
On that day you will say, “I thank you, Lord, because you were angry with me, but you turned away your anger and comforted me.”
Look, I trust in God my Savior and will not tremble, because the Lord is my strength and my glory, and he will be my salvation.
You will draw water with joy from the spring of salvation.
On that day you will say, “Give thanks to the Lord and call on his name. Make his deeds known among the nations. Remember that his name is mighty.”
Sing to the Lord, for he has done majestic things. This is known throughout the earth.
Rejoice and give praise, inhabitant of Zion, for great is the Holy One of Israel who is among you.
The pronouncement concerning Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
Raise a banner on the bare mountains. Raise your voice to them. Wave your hand so that the rulers may enter your gates.
I have commanded my consecrated ones and summoned my warriors in my anger, those who grow strong in my majesty.
The sound of a tumult on the mountain, like that of many peoples! The sound of a tumult of kingdoms, of nations gathering together! The mighty Lord is mustering armies for battle.
They come from far away, from the ends of heaven—the Lord and the instruments of his anger—to destroy the whole earth.
Wail, for the day of the Lord is near! It will come suddenly like plunder.
Therefore all hands will grow weak, and every human heart will melt.
They will be terrified, and pangs and pains like those of a woman in labor will seize them. They will look at one another in astonishment; their faces will be like flames.
Look, the day of the Lord is coming, with no remedy in it, cruel and burning with his anger, to make the earth a wasteland and destroy its sinners from it.
For the stars of heaven and their hosts will not shine. The sun will grow dark as it rises, and the moon's light will not shine.
I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their wrongdoing. I will put an end to the arrogance of the boastful and bring down the pride of the powerful.
I will make a man more precious than gold, a human being more precious than the gold of Ophir.
Therefore I will shake the heavens, and the earth will move from its place at the rebuke of the mighty Lord, on the day of his fierce anger.
They will be like fleeing gazelles and like sheep with no one to gather them. Each will turn back to his own people, and each will flee to his own land.
Everyone who is found will be stabbed, and everyone who joins them will fall by the sword.
Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses will be plundered, and their wives will be raped.
Look, I am stirring up the Medes against you. They place no value on silver and have no desire for gold.
The bows of the young men will be broken. They will have no mercy on the fruit of the womb, and their eyes will have no pity on their children.
Babylon, the might of kingdoms and the glory of the Chaldeans' pride, will be like Sodom and Gomorrah when God overthrew them.
It will never be inhabited or settled in, from generation to generation. Arabs will not camp there, and shepherds will not pasture their flocks there.
Instead, wild animals will lie down there, and their houses will be filled with echoes. Ostriches will dwell there, and demons will dance there.
Sirens will call to one another in their courts, and jackals in their luxurious palaces. Its time is near, and its days will no longer be prolonged.
For the Lord has compassion on Jacob and again chooses Israel. He will let them remain in their land. Settlers will join them and become part of the house of Jacob.

The peoples will take them and bring them to their land. The house of Israel will possess them in the Lord's land as male and female slaves. They will take their captors captive and rule over those who enslaved them.
And on the day when the LORD gives you rest from your sorrow, your distress, and the harsh slavery to which you were subjected,
You will take up this saying against the king of Babylon and say, “How the ruler has ceased, and the taskmaster has ceased!”
The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked man and the scepter of the ruler,
who struck peoples in fury with unrelenting blows, ruled nations in anger, and pursued them without pity.
The whole earth is at rest and quiet; it rejoices with songs of praise.
Even the cypresses and the cedars of Lebanon rejoice over you: “Since you lay down, no one has come up against us to cut us down.”
Sheol below was stirred up to meet you at your arrival. It roused the mighty ones against you, and all the rulers of the earth; it raised all the kings of the nations from their thrones.
They will answer and say to you, “You too have become weak like us! You have been handed over to us!”
Your splendor has gone down to Sheol, and your harp has died. Maggots will be spread beneath you, and worms will cover you.
How you have fallen from heaven! Wail at dawn! You have fallen to the earth, you who insulted the nations!
You said in your heart, “I will ascend to heaven and raise my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the high mountains in the far reaches of the north.”
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds and make myself like the Most High.”
But now you will go down to Sheol, to the bottom of the pit.
All who see you will stare at you and consider you, saying, “Is this the man who shook the earth and made kingdoms tremble?”
He made the world desolate like a wilderness, overthrew its towns, and did not release his prisoners.
All the kings of the nations lie in honor, each in his own tomb.
But you have been thrown out of your grave like a despised shoot, like the clothing of the slain, those killed by the sword who descend to the stones of the pit, like trampled corpses.
You will not rejoice with them in the grave, because you ruined your land and killed your people. An evil offspring will never rise again.
Prepare slaughter for his sons because of their father's wickedness, so that they do not rise up, take possession of the earth, and fill the face of the world with war.
“I will rise against them,” says the mighty Lord, “and destroy Babylon's name, her offspring, her lineage, and her family,” says the Lord.
“I will make it a possession for hedgehogs and pools of water, and I will sweep it away with the broom of destruction,” says the mighty Lord.
The LORD Almighty has sworn and said, “As I have planned, so it will be; as I have decided, so it will stand:
That I will break the Assyrian in my land and trample him on my mountains. His yoke will pass away from them, and his bondage will pass away from their shoulders.
This is the plan I have devised against the whole earth, and this is the hand raised against all the nations.
The LORD Almighty has decided—who can undo it? His hand is raised—who can turn it back?
The oracle concerning Philistia. This oracle came in the year that King Ahaz died.
Do not rejoice, all Philistia, because the rod of your oppressor has been broken. For a viper will come out from the serpent’s root, and its fruit will be a flying serpent.
The firstborn of the poor will graze, and the afflicted will lie down peacefully. I will kill your root with famine, and whatever remains of you will be killed.
Wail, towns! Lament, city! All Philistia is thrown into turmoil, because smoke is coming from the north, and no one is alone at his festivals.
What answer shall we give the messenger of the nations? That the Lord establishes Zion’s foundations, and the afflicted of his people will take refuge in her.
The oracle concerning Moab. In the night Moab’s city was plundered, and they were stunned. In the night Moab’s walls were plundered, and they were bewildered.
They went up to the house of Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and Medeba. Every head is bald, and every beard is shaved.
In its streets they have wrapped themselves in sackcloth. On the rooftops and in the streets everyone wails and goes down weeping.
Heshbon and Elealeh will wail, and their voices will be heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore Moab’s mighty men will cry out, and its own soul will cry out for it.

My heart will wail for Moab, for its fugitives as far as Zoar, the three-year-old heifer. For they will climb the ascent of Luhith weeping, and on the road to Horonaim they will raise a cry of destruction.
For the waters of Nimrim will disappear, because the hay has dried up, the young grass has withered, and there is no greenery.
Therefore what remained has gone across, and they will carry their possessions across the Wadi of Willows.
For wailing has gone around Moab’s border. Its wailing reaches as far as Eglaim, and its lament reaches Beer-elim.
For the waters of Dibon are filled with blood, because I will bring still more upon Dibon, and [?] upon those who escape from Moab and upon the remnant of the land.
Send the son of the ruler of the land from the rock of the wilderness to the mountain of Daughter Zion.
It will be like a bird moving its nest, and the daughters of Moab will be abandoned at the crossing of the Arnon.
Offer counsel and make a decision. Make your shade like night at midday. Hide those who wander, and do not expose those who are scattered.
Let Moab’s scattered people live with you. Be a refuge for them from the plunderer. For the dust has come to an end, the plunderer has vanished, and the trampler has disappeared from the land.
A throne will be established in kindness, and in David’s tent one will sit on it faithfully: a judge who seeks justice and is quick to do what is right.
We have heard of Moab’s pride, how very proud it has become—its pride, its arrogance, and its might. Its diviners did not predict this about it.
Therefore Moab will wail, and all of it will wail over Moab. You will groan like the sick over the foundations of the walls being demolished.

For Heshbon’s fields have been laid waste. The warriors of the nations have cut off the shoots of Sibmah’s vine. They reached as far as Jazer and wandered into the wilderness; its tendrils stretched out and crossed the sea.

Therefore I will weep for you with Jazer’s weeping, vines of Sibmah. I will drench you with your tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, because the trampler has fallen upon your harvest and your grape gathering.

Joy and gladness will pass away from the fruitful fields. No one will rejoice in the fruitful fields or press wine in the winepress, and no treader will tread, because I will put an end to the treader.
Therefore my belly will sound like a lyre for Moab, and my inward parts for the wall being demolished.
When Moab sees that he has worn himself out on the high places, he will come to the sanctuary to pray, but he will not be able to.
This is the word that the Lord spoke about Moab in earlier times.

Now the Lord has spoken and said: Within three years, counted like the years of a hired worker, Moab’s glory will be brought low, along with its great multitude of people. A small, insignificant remnant will remain, not many.
The oracle concerning Damascus. Look, Damascus will cease to be a city and will become a ruin and a heap of rubble.
The towns of Aroer will be abandoned and will belong to flocks, which will lie down in them with no one to frighten them.
Strength will disappear from Ephraim, and kingship from Damascus. The remnant of Ephraim will be like the glory of the Israelites, says the Lord Almighty.
On that day Jacob’s glory will be diminished, and the fatness of his body will waste away.
It will be like someone gathering a harvest of standing grain and reaping ears of grain with his arm. It will be like someone gleaning ears of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
Gleanings will remain in it, as when an olive tree is beaten: two or three olives at the top of a branch, and four or five on its boughs, says the Lord, the God of Israel.
On that day a person will trust in his Maker, and his eyes will look toward the Holy One of Israel.
He will not rely on the altars his hands made, the work of his fingers, nor will he look to idols and objects of worship.
On that day his fortified towns will be like the hollow of the forest and the treetop [?], abandoned before the Israelites; and you will become a ruin.
You have forgotten God your Savior and have not remembered the Mighty One who strengthens you. Therefore you will plant a delightful planting and sow it with foreign shoots.
On the day you plant it, blossoms will come out, and in the morning you will make your seed sprout, like a field at harvest on a day of sorrow, and like human pain.
Woe to the multitude of many peoples, whose sound goes out like the sound of the seas, and to the tumult of nations, like the sound of mighty waters!
He will rebuke it, and it will flee far away and be driven like dust on the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before a whirlwind.
At evening, look—sudden destruction! Before morning comes, nothing will remain. This is the share of those who trample us and the portion of those who plunder us.
Woe to the land of the shadow of wings, beyond the rivers of Cush,

Who sends envoys by sea, in papyrus vessels over the surface of the water. Go, swift messengers, to a people stripped and uprooted, to a people feared far and wide, a people ravaged and trampled, whose land the rivers have plundered.
All you inhabitants of the world who live on the earth: when the mountains raise a signal, you will see it, and when the trumpet sounds, you will hear it.
For this is what the Lord said to me: I will remain quiet and watch from my dwelling, like clear heat over the river and like a cloud of dew on a harvest day.
For before the harvest, when the growth is complete and the blossom has finished and become young fruit, he will cut off the tendrils with a pruning knife, and remove and cut away the shoots.
They will be left together for the birds of the mountains and the animals of the earth. The birds will gather over them, and all the animals of the earth will rage over them.

On that day a people stripped and uprooted, a people feared far and wide, a people ravaged and trampled, whose land the rivers have plundered, will bring offerings to the Lord Almighty, to the place of the name of the Lord Almighty, to Mount Zion.
The pronouncement concerning Egypt. Look, the Lord is riding on swift clouds and entering Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble before him, and Egypt’s heart will melt within it.
I will stir up Egyptian against Egyptian, and each man will fight against his brother and each man against his neighbor, city against city and kingdom against kingdom.
Egypt’s spirit will fail within it, and I will confound its counsel. They will consult idols, magicians, mediums, and diviners.
I will hand the Egyptians over to harsh masters, and a powerful king will rule over them, says the Lord Almighty.
The waters will disappear from the sea, and the river will become parched and dry.
The rivers will disappear, and the mighty rivers will dwindle and dry up. Reeds, rushes, and papyrus will wither.
The vegetation beside the river and at the river’s mouth, and everything sown along the riverbank, will dry up, be swept away, and no longer be found.
The fishermen will lament, and those who cast hooks into the river will sit in mourning. Those who spread nets over the surface of the water have grown weak.
The workers in flax who comb and weave for rejoicing will be ashamed.
All who make beer for people to drink will be brought low.
The princes of Zoan have become foolish. The wise men who advise Pharaoh give foolish advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, ‘We are wise men and descendants of ancient kings’?
Where are your wise men? Let them tell you, and let them know what the Lord Almighty has planned against Egypt.
The princes of Zoan have become foolish; the princes of Memphis have become arrogant. The cornerstones of Egypt’s tribes have led her astray.
The Lord has mixed a spirit of confusion within Egypt and has led Egypt astray in all its deeds, as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.
The Egyptian will have no one to do anything—head or tail, tail or head.
On that day Egypt will be like women, afraid and trembling before the raised hand of the Lord Almighty, which he raises against it.
The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt. Whenever anyone mentions it to Egypt, it will be frightened because of the plan that the Lord Almighty has devised against it.
On that day there will be five towns in the land of Egypt speaking the language of Canaan and swearing by the Lord Almighty. One of them will be called Heres.
On that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the Lord beside its border.

It will be a sign and a witness to the Lord Almighty in the land of Egypt. For they will cry out before the Lord because of their oppressors, and he will send them a savior and a judge, and he will rescue them.
The Lord will make himself known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know the Lord on that day. They will offer sacrifices and fine flour, and they will make vows to the Lord and fulfill them.
The Lord will strike the Egyptians with a blow and heal them. They will return to the Lord, and he will answer them and heal them.
On that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria and from Assyria to Egypt. The Assyrians will enter Egypt, and the Egyptians will enter Assyria, and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians.
On that day Israel will be one of three, along with the Egyptians and the Assyrians, a blessing in the midst of the earth.
The Lord Almighty has blessed him and said, “Blessed are my people in Egypt, the work of my hands in Assyria, and Israel my inheritance.”
In the year when Tartan came to Ashdod, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, he fought against Ashdod and captured it.

At that time the Lord spoke through Isaiah the prophet, son of Amoz, and said to him, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and your sandals from your feet.” He did so and walked barefoot and naked.
The Lord said, “Just as my servant Isaiah has walked barefoot and naked, so there will be signs and wonders for three years concerning Egypt and Cush.
So the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the captives of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, and Egypt’s nakedness will be exposed.”
They will be shattered and ashamed because of Cush, their confidence, and Egypt, their glory.

On that day the inhabitants of this coastland will say, “This is what has become of those we trusted, to whom we fled for help and for deliverance from the king of Assyria! How, then, will we escape?”
The pronouncement concerning the wilderness of the sea. Like a whirlwind from the south, it races out of the wilderness and comes from a distant land.
A harsh vision has been shown to us: the oppressor oppresses, and the plunderer plunders. Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media! I have put an end to all her groaning.
Because of this, my loins are filled with trembling, and pangs have seized me like the pangs of a woman giving birth. I tremble so that I cannot hear; I am so distressed that I cannot see.
My heart wandered, and pains shook me. The beautiful things I desired have become a terror to me.
Prepare the tables! Post the lookouts! Eat and drink! Rise, commanders! Oil the shields!
For this is what the Lord said to me: “Go, station a lookout, and let him report whatever he sees.”
He saw a mounted company of two horsemen, a rider on a donkey and a rider on a camel, and he listened very carefully.
The lookout called out in my hearing and said, “Lord, I stand continually by day, and I stand at my watch all through the nights.”
Look, a man is coming from among the mounted riders! He answered and said, “Babylon has fallen, has fallen! All her carved gods have been shattered on the ground.”
Who has reaped, and who has worn down the threshing floor? What I heard from the Lord, the God of Israel, I have told you.
The oracle concerning Dumah. Someone calls to me from Seir: “Watchman in the night!”
The watchman said, “Morning is coming, and also night. If you wish to inquire, inquire; you are coming back again.”
The oracle concerning Arabia. In the evening you will spend the night in the forest, on the road of Duranim.
Bring water to meet the thirsty, inhabitants of the land of the south. Meet the fugitives with your bread.
For they have scattered before the sword, before the sharpened blade, before the drawn bow, and before the fury of battle.
For this is what the Lord said to me: “At the end of a year, counted like the years of a hired worker, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end.
The remaining number of archers, the warriors of the people of Kedar, will be few, for the Lord, the God of Israel, has spoken.”
The pronouncement concerning the Valley of Vision. What is the matter with you here, that all of you have gone up to the rooftops?
The city is filled with turmoil; the mighty city is filled with noise. Your slain were not slain by the sword, nor were they killed in battle.
All your rulers fled together; they were captured by the bow. Those who remained in you were captured together, though they had fled far away.
Therefore I said, “Leave me alone to weep bitterly. Do not insist on comforting me over the destruction of the daughter of my people.”
For the Lord God Almighty has a day of turmoil, trampling, and weeping in the Valley of Vision. The wall is breached, and a cry goes up over the mountains.
Elam took up the quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen, and Shur uncovered the shields.
The choicest of your valleys will be full of chariots, and horsemen will draw up in formation at the gates.
Judah will uncover the ranks, and on that day you will see the weapons of the House of the Forest.
You saw that the breaches in the City of David were many, and you gathered the water of the lower pool.
You filled the houses of Jerusalem, and you demolished houses to strengthen the wall.
You made reservoirs between the walls for the water of the old pool, but you did not look to its maker or consider the one who formed it long ago.
On that day the Lord God Almighty called for weeping and lamentation, for shaving heads and putting on sackcloth.
But look: pleasure and joy, slaughtering cattle and slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine! “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
The Lord Almighty revealed this in my hearing and said, “You will not remove this sin from yourselves until you die,” says the Lord God Almighty.
This is what the Lord Almighty says: “Go to this steward, to Shebna, the administrator of the household, and say to him:
What are you doing here, and what do you have here, that you have hewn out a tomb for yourself here? He hews out his tomb on the height and carves his dwelling in the rock.
Look, the Lord will hurl you away, man, and make you wander far away.
He will squeeze you tightly like a ball in a wide-open land. There you will die, and there will be your glorious chariot, the shame of your master's house.
I will bring you down from your honored position and overthrow you from your office.
On that day, says the Lord, I will call my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.

I will clothe him in your tunic and fasten your sash around him. I will place your authority in his hands, and he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the men of the house of Judah.
He will put the keys of the house of David on his shoulder. He will open, and no one will shut; he will shut, and no one will open.
I will fasten him like a peg in a secure place, and he will become a throne of honor for his father's household.
They will hang on him all the glory of his father's house, honored and praised, and every small vessel, from instruments of song to instruments of the lyre.
On that day, says the Lord Almighty, the peg driven into a secure place will be pulled out. It will be overturned and fall, and the load placed on it will perish, for the Lord has spoken.
The oracle concerning Tyre. Wail, ships of Tarshish, because it has been plundered, without a house or harbor [?]. From the land of Kittim it has been revealed to us.
Be silent, inhabitants of the island! The merchant of Sidon who crosses the sea has filled you.
Across the great waters came the merchant's seed; the river's harvest was her revenue. She became a marketplace for the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea, the stronghold of the sea, has said, "I have not been in labor or given birth. I have not raised troops or brought up virgins."
When Egypt hears, anguish will seize them, as at the news of Tyre.
Cross over to Tarshish! Wail, inhabitants of the island!
This is your strong city, dating from the earliest days. Her feet will go ahead of her, so that she may settle far away.
Who planned this against Tyre, the giver of crowns, whose merchants are princes and whose traders are the honored people of the earth?
The Lord Almighty planned it, to abolish the glory of every power and to disgrace all the honored people of the earth.
Flow through your land like a river, daughter of Tarshish! There is no longer anyone to oppress you.
He raised his hand over the sea and shook kingdoms. The Lord commanded concerning Canaan that its strongholds be destroyed.
He said, "You will no longer grow strong, oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon. Get up and cross over to Kittim. Even there you will have no rest."
Look at the land of the Chaldeans! This is the people that did not exist. The Assyrian gave it over to the wind and set up siege towers. They stripped its fortifications and made it a ruin.
Wail, ships of Tarshish, because your stronghold has been plundered!
On that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the lifetime of one king. After seventy years they will sing to Tyre the song of a prostitute.
Take a lyre and go around the city, forgotten prostitute! Play skillfully and sing many songs, so that you may be remembered.
After seventy years the Lord will visit Tyre and restore her to her earnings, and she will prostitute herself with all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.

Her merchandise and her earnings will be holy to the Lord. They will not be put in a treasury or stored away. Instead, her merchandise will belong to those who dwell before the Lord, so that they may eat their fill and clothe her aged people.
Look, the Lord is devastating the earth and breaking it open, overturning its surface and scattering its inhabitants.
The people will be like the priest, the servant like his master, the maidservant like her mistress, the buyer like the seller, the borrower like the lender, and the debtor like his creditor.
The earth will be utterly devastated and completely plundered, because the Lord has spoken this word.
The earth laments and sits in mourning. The world laments, sits in grief, and mourns. The heights of the earth lament.
The earth has become like its inhabitants, because they have transgressed the law, changed the commandment, and annulled the everlasting covenant.
Because of these things the earth will sit in mourning, and all its inhabitants will be condemned. Because of this all the inhabitants of the earth will be devastated, and few people will remain.
The grain sits in mourning, the vines lament, and all the joyful-hearted sigh.
Joy has ceased, and so have the tambourines. The sound of rejoicing has fallen silent. Joy has ceased, and so have the lyres.
They will not drink wine with singing. Strong drink will taste bitter to those who drink it.
The city has been plundered, and all the winepress houses have been shut.
There is wailing over the wine in the streets. All joy has ceased, and the earth's gladness has passed away.
Destruction remains in the city, and misery will cut down its gates.
This is how it will be throughout the earth among the peoples: like the beating of an olive tree, like the gleaning when the grape harvest is finished.
They will raise their voices and give praise for the majesty of the Lord; they will shout for joy from the sea.
Therefore praise the Lord with songs of praise, and on the islands of the sea praise the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.

From the ends of the earth we have heard a song: "Strength to the righteous one," who says, "A mystery for me, a mystery for me! Woe to me! The wicked have acted wickedly; the wicked have committed wickedness."
Terror, the pit, and the snare are upon you, inhabitants of the earth!

Whoever flees from the sound of terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the snare. For the floodgates on high have been opened, and the foundations of the earth have shaken.
The earth will shake violently; the earth will sway wildly; the earth will totter greatly.
The earth will reel like a drunkard and sway like a hammock. Its wickedness will weigh heavily on it, and it will fall and never rise again.
On that day the Lord will punish the hosts on high in the heights, and the kings of the earth on the earth.
They will gather in groups around the prisoner in the pit and be counted among the imprisoned; after many days they will be released.
The moon will be disgraced and the sun ashamed, for the Lord Almighty has become king on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and he will be glorified before his holy ones.
Lord, you are my God. I will exalt you and give thanks to your name, for you have done a wonderful thing and carried out a faithful purpose from long ago. Amen.
For you have made a city into a heap and a fortified city into a ruin. The foreigners' temple will never be rebuilt in the city.
Therefore many peoples will glorify you, and the city of mighty nations will fear you.
For you have been a helper to the poor and an aid to the afflicted in his distress, a shelter from the storm and shade from the heat. For the blast of the mighty is like a storm against a wall.
As shade relieves the heat, the pride of foreigners will be brought low. As heat is subdued by the shade of clouds, the [?] of the mighty will be brought low.
On this mountain the Lord Almighty will prepare for all peoples a rich banquet and a banquet of aged drink, and rich food that [?], rich and strong.
On this mountain the face of the ruler who ruled over all the nations will be swallowed up, along with the sacrifice that was slaughtered over all the nations.
Death will be swallowed up in victory forever. The Lord God Almighty will wipe away tears from every face, and he will remove his people's disgrace from the whole earth, for the Lord has spoken.
You will say on that day, “This is the Lord our God, for whom we have waited to save us. This is the Lord our God, for whom we have waited. Let us rejoice and be glad in his salvation.”
For the Lord's hand will rest on this mountain, and Moab will be trampled beneath him, as straw is trampled on a threshing floor.
He will spread out his hands in its midst as a swimmer spreads out his hands to swim, and he will bring down his strength with the sweep of his hands.
He will bring down the fortified stronghold of your walls, lower it, and bring it to the ground, down to the dust.
On that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: “A city whose salvation is strong! Set up a wall and an outer wall.”
Open the gates so that the righteous people who keep faith may enter.
You who guard faithfully will preserve peace for us, because we have placed our hope in you.
The Lord forever and ever, for the Lord God is mighty forever.
For he has brought low those who dwell on high. He will bring the strong city down to the ground and bring it down to the dust.
The feet of the afflicted and the footsteps of the poor will trample it.
The path is straight for the poor, and the road of the righteous is straight and smooth.
Indeed, Lord, we have waited for the path of your judgments. Our souls have longed for your name and your remembrance.
My soul has longed for you in the night, and my spirit within me seeks you early. For as your judgments come upon the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
Let the wicked man be removed, so that he may not learn righteousness. There is rebuke in an established land, and they will not see the Lord's majesty.
Lord, they will not see when your hands are raised. They will see the people's zeal and be ashamed, and like a furnace you will consume your enemies.
Lord, you will preserve peace for us, for you have made provision for us according to all our deeds.
Lord our God, masters other than you have ruled over us, but we will remember your name alone.
The dead do not live, and the mighty do not rise. Therefore you punished them and [?] them, and destroyed every memory of them.
You have increased the nation, Lord; you have increased the nation. You have withdrawn and driven away all the ends of the earth.
LORD, in distress they sought you, and in confinement they whispered of your discipline.
Like a pregnant woman near delivery, writhing and crying out in her labor pains, so we were before you, LORD.
We conceived and suffered labor pains like women giving birth to wind. Save us, so that we do not perish in the land and the inhabitants of the world do not fall.
Your dead will live, and their corpses will rise. Those who sleep in the dust will awaken and sing praises, for your dew is a dew of light, and the land of the mighty will be overthrown.
Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you. Hide for a little while, until my anger has passed.
For look, the Lord is coming out from his place to punish the inhabitant of the earth for his wrongdoing. The earth will uncover its blood and will no longer conceal its slain.
On that day the Lord will punish Leviathan, the [?] serpent, and Leviathan, the twisting serpent, with his harsh, great, and mighty sword. He will kill the dragon that is in the sea.
On that day, sing to the vineyard of wine!
I, the Lord, guard it. I water it continually and watch over it. By night and by day I guard it.
You have no wall. But whoever puts brushwood and thorns in you—I will blow upon it at close quarters and burn it all together.
Or let him take hold of my strength, and I will make peace with him; peace I will make with him.
Those from the root of Jacob will put out branches; Israel will sprout, and they will fill the face of the world with fruit.
Did he strike him as the one who struck him did? Did he kill him as the one who killed him did?
With the measure he measured, you will judge him, on the threshing floor, with his harsh wind on a hot day.

Therefore Jacob's wrongdoing will be forgiven through this, and through all these fruits his sin will pass away: when he makes all the altar stones like crumbling chalk stones, idols and objects of worship will no longer stand.
For the strong city stands alone, ruined and abandoned, desolate like the wilderness. There a calf will graze; there it will feed and consume its shoots.

When the harvest dries, they will be broken. Women who come will set it alight. For this is not a people with understanding. Therefore its Maker will not have mercy on it, and the one who formed it will not have compassion on it.
On that day the Lord will thresh from the channel of the River to the stream of Egypt, and you, children of Israel, will be gathered one by one.

On that day a great trumpet will be sounded. Those who were lost in the land of Egypt and those who were scattered in the land of Assyria will come and worship the Lord in the Lord's land, on his holy mountain in Jerusalem.
Woe to the proud crown of drunken Ephraim, and to the despised wreath, the strength of his glory, at the head of the valley of the prosperous, who are overcome by wine!
Look, the Lord's might and strength are like a hailstorm, like a destructive tempest, and like a downpour of abundant, sweeping waters. Bring it down to the ground with your hand.
The proud crown of drunken Ephraim will be trampled underfoot.

The despised wreath, the strength of his glory, at the head of the valley of the prosperous, will be like an early fig before summer: as soon as someone sees it, he swallows it while it is still in his hand.
On that day the mighty LORD will be a crown of strength and a glorious garland for the remnant of his people,
a spirit of justice for the one who sits in judgment, and courage for those who turn the battle back from the gate.

These too have gone astray through wine and wandered through strong drink. Priests and prophets have gone astray through strong drink; they have been swallowed up by wine and staggered from strong drink. They have gone astray in drunkenness and eaten gluttonously.
For all the tables are filled with vomit and filth, leaving no place clean.
Whom will he teach knowledge, and whom will he make understand the message? Those weaned from milk and taken from the breasts?
For it is filth upon filth, filth upon filth, vomit upon vomit, vomit upon vomit, a little there and a little there.
For with halting speech and in another language I will speak to this people.
I said to them, “This is my rest: give rest to the weary. This is quiet.” But they were unwilling to listen.

The word of the Lord became for them filth upon filth, filth upon filth, vomit upon vomit, vomit upon vomit, a little there and a little there, so that they would turn back, fall backward, be broken, be trapped, and be captured.
Therefore hear the word of the Lord, you scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem.

Because you said, “We have established a covenant with death and made an agreement with Sheol. When the sweeping scourge passes through, it will not come upon us, because we have placed our trust in falsehood and hidden ourselves in lies.”
Therefore this is what the Lord God says: “Look, I am setting a stone in Zion, a chosen stone, precious at the corner, the chief stone of the foundation wall. Whoever believes will not be afraid.
I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the weight. Hail will beat down the false hope, and water will sweep away the hiding place.
Your covenant with death will be annulled, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the sweeping scourge passes through, you will be trampled by it.
Whenever it passes through, it will carry you away, for morning after morning it will pass through, by day and by night. Merely understanding the report will bring terror.
For the garment is too short to cover him, and the covering is too narrow and does not suffice.
For the Lord will rise on the mountain at the breach; he will rage as in the valley of Gibeon, to do his deeds—strange are his deeds—and to carry out his works—strange are his works.
Now do not mock, lest your punishments grow more severe, for I have heard from the mighty Lord of complete destruction and decrees against the whole earth.
Listen and hear my voice; pay attention and hear what I say.
Does the farmer plow all day to sow, breaking up and leveling his land?
When he has leveled its surface, does he not scatter black cumin, sow cumin, and plant wheat, barley, and spelt within its boundaries?
Let them instruct him in God's judgment and give praise.
For black cumin is not threshed with a threshing sledge, nor is a wagon wheel rolled over cumin. Rather, black cumin is beaten out with a staff, and cumin with sticks.
Grain is threshed for our sake, for he does not keep threshing it forever. With the many revolutions of his wagon wheels and with his hooves, they crush it.
This too came from the mighty Lord: wonderful counsel. He has made instruction great.
Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the city where David camped! Add year to year; let the festivals be celebrated.
I will distress Ariel, and there will be groaning and lamentation, and she will be like Ariel.
I will encamp around you in a circle, hem you in with a siegework, and set up a watch against you.
You will be brought low and speak from the dust. Your words will chirp from the dust, and your voice will be heard from the earth like a spirit's voice. Your words will chirp from the dust.
The multitude of those who trample you will become like fine sand, and the multitude of your mighty attackers like chaff that blows away. It will happen suddenly, in an instant.
You will be visited by the mighty Lord with earthquakes, thunder, a great noise, lightning flashes, a whirlwind, and a flame of consuming fire.
The multitude of all the nations that wage war against Ariel, and all the armies and crowds that besiege her, will become like a dream, like a vision in the night.

It will be like a hungry person who dreams that he is eating, but when he wakes, he is exhausted and still hungry. So will it be with the multitude of all the nations that wage war against Mount Zion.
Be astonished and amazed; be bewildered and stagger! They are drunk, but not from wine; they wander, but not from strong drink.
For the Lord has poured over them a spirit of deep sleep, and it has overwhelmed their eyes, the prophets, and their leaders who see hidden things.

The vision of them all will become for them like the words of a sealed book. When they give it to someone who can read, they will say to him, “Read this,” and he will say, “I cannot, because it is sealed.”
They will give the book to someone who cannot read and say to him, “Read this,” and he will say, “I cannot read.”
The Lord said, “Because this people draws near with its mouth and honors me with its lips, while its heart is far from me, and their fear of me has become a matter of human commands and teaching,

therefore, look, I will once again set this people apart through a wonder and a marvel. The wisdom of their wise people will perish, and the understanding of their discerning people will be taken away.”
Woe to those who twist away from the Lord to hide their plans, whose deeds are done in darkness, and who say, “Who sees us, or who knows?”

Why are we being turned upside down? You are regarded as the potter's clay. Does something made say to its maker, “You did not make me”? Or does something molded say to the one who molded it, “You did not mold me skillfully”?
Look, in just a little while Lebanon will become a fruitful field, and the fruitful field will be regarded as a forest.
On that day the deaf will hear the words of the book, and out of darkness and gloom the eyes of the blind will see.
The humble will find increasing joy in the Lord, and unfortunate people will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
For the oppressor has passed away, the mocker has come to an end, and all who stir up injustice have perished—
those who make people guilty by a word, set a trap for someone who rebukes them, and turn the righteous aside in darkness.
Therefore this is what the Lord, who redeemed Abraham, says concerning the house of Jacob: Jacob will no longer be ashamed, and his face will no longer blush.
When his children see the work of my hands in his midst, they will honor my name as holy. They will honor the Holy One of Jacob as holy and exalt the God of Israel.
The foolish, whose spirits had gone astray, will come to understand, and the senseless will learn to obey.”
Woe to the rebellious children, says the Lord, who made plans that did not come from me and poured out drink offerings that were not prompted by my Spirit, adding sin to sin.
They went down to Egypt without asking me, to find strength in Pharaoh's strength and shelter in Egypt's shadow.
Pharaoh’s strength will become a source of shame for you, and shelter in Egypt’s shadow a source of humiliation.
For he and his officials are in Zoan, and his messengers will toil [?]
among a people who are of no use to them, bringing neither help nor benefit, but only shame and disgrace.

An oracle concerning the beasts of the south. Through a land of distress and hardship, where there are lions and lion cubs, and among them asps and flying vipers, they carry their wealth on the backs of young donkeys and their treasures on the backs of camels to a people who cannot benefit them.
The Egyptians offer help that is empty and deceptive. Therefore I have declared concerning them that this confidence in them is empty.
Now come, write on these tablets and in the book of their covenant, so that it may remain for the last day as a testimony forever and ever.
For they are a rebellious people, lying children, children unwilling to listen to the Lord’s law.
They said to the seers, “Do not see,” and to the prophets, “Do not prophesy rebukes to us. Speak ambiguously to us, and see false visions for us.”
Turn aside from the road, turn away from the paths, and remove the Holy One of Israel from us.
Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says: Because you have rejected this word, trusted in oppression, grumbled, and relied on it,
therefore this sin will be for you like a collapsing breach, like a high wall whose collapse comes suddenly.

Its breaking will be like the breaking of a potter's vessel, shattered without mercy, so that among its fragments no shard can be found with which to take fire from the hearth or scoop water from a cistern.
For this is what the Holy One of Israel says: When you return and rest, you will be saved; in quietness and hope will be your strength. But you were unwilling.
You said, “No! We will ride on horses and flee on swift mounts.” Therefore you will flee, and your pursuers will be swift.
A thousand will flee at the rebuke of one, and at the rebuke of five you will flee, until you are left like wild donkeys on a mountaintop and like a signal on a hill.
For the Lord will wait to show you mercy, and he will rise up to have compassion on you. For the Lord is God the judge, and blessed are all who wait for him.
For the people will dwell in Zion and Jerusalem. You will weep no more. He will surely have mercy at the sound of your cry; when he hears, he will answer you.
The Lord will give you bread in distress and water in distress. He will no longer gather together those who mislead you, and your eyes will see those who mislead you.
Your ears will hear a word behind you saying, “This is the way; walk in it, and do not turn aside to the right or to the left.”
You will defile the silver plating of your idols and the covering of their cast gold images. You will scatter them like a washerwoman's wastewater and cast them out like spittle.
Rain will be given for the seed you sow in the ground, and the grain produced from the earth's seed will be rich and plentiful. On that day your livestock's pasture will be in a fertile place.
The oxen and donkeys that work the ground will eat warm mixed fodder that has been tossed up with a shovel and a winnowing fork.
On every lofty mountain and every high hill, streams of water will flow on the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, on the day when the Lord binds up his people's brokenness and heals the pain of their wound.
Look, the name of the Lord comes from far away. His anger burns, and his burden is glorious. His lips are full of anger, and his tongue is like a consuming fire.
His breath is like a sweeping torrent, reaching up to the neck, to throw the nations into turmoil because of their empty delusions and the misleading bridle on the peoples' jaws.
Praise will be a crown for you, consecrated at the feast, and gladness of heart like that of someone walking joyfully to come to the mountain of the Lord, to the Mighty One of Israel.
The Lord will make his glorious voice heard and display the blow of his arm, with furious anger and a flame of consuming fire, with a battering storm and hailstones.
For the Assyrian will be shattered before the majesty of the Lord and struck with a rod.
In all his deeds there will be a rod of subjugation, which the Lord will lay upon him, with tambourines and lyres; and he will fight against him in fierce battle.

For his fuel has been prepared since ancient days. It too has been prepared to reign, and it has made its dwelling deep and wide. There is much wood and fire, and the breath of the Lord is like a torrent, with sulfur burning in it.
