Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help and rely on horses, who rely on many chariots and on horsemen because they are very strong, but have not relied on the Holy One of Israel and have not sought the Lord.
In his wisdom he brought disaster and did not take back his words. He rose against the house of evildoers and against the help of those who practice injustice.

The Egyptians are human beings, not gods, and their horses are flesh, not spirit. The Lord will stretch out his hand, and the helper will be overthrown; the one being helped will also fall, and all of them will perish together.

For this is what the Lord said to me: As a lion or a young lion growls over what it has killed, and a crowd of shepherds shouts at it, yet it does not fear their voices or become alarmed at their numbers, so the mighty Lord will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its heights.
Like birds flying overhead, so the mighty Lord will shield Jerusalem. He will shield and deliver it; he will support and help it.
Return, children of Israel, you who have intensified your rebellion.
For on that day people will reject the idols of silver and gold that your hands made for you as a sin.
The Assyrian will fall by a sword, a sword not belonging to men; a sword not belonging to warriors will devour him. He will flee before the sword, and his young men will become a sign.
The rocky height of his dwelling will pass away, and his nobles will be shattered by a sign, says the Lord, whose light is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
Look, kings will rule in righteousness, and rulers will exercise authority with justice.
A man will be like a shelter from the wind and a refuge from the storm, like a stream of water in a thirsty place and the shade of a mighty rock in a weary land.
The eyes of those who see will not be dimmed, and the ears of those who hear will listen attentively.
The heart of the foolish will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerer will be quick to speak clearly.
They will no longer call a fool a ruler, nor will they call a worthless person a savior.
For the fool speaks foolishness, and his heart devises injustice, to practice godlessness and speak of error, to leave the hungry person empty and withhold drink from the thirsty.
The worthless person's tools are evil. He devises schemes to ruin the poor with lying words, and the word of the afflicted in court [?].
But the noble person plans noble things, and he will stand firm in noble things.
Wealthy women, rise and hear my voice! Confident daughters, listen to my words!
You confident women will tremble for a year, because the grape harvest has failed; it has been delayed and has not come.
Tremble, wealthy women! Shake, you confident women! Strip yourselves bare and tie sackcloth around your waists.
Beat your breasts for the green growth of the field and for the vine and its fruit.
Thorns and brushwood will grow on the land of my people, in all the houses of joy and in the strong city.

For the temple has been forgotten, and the city's stronghold has been abandoned. The beautiful houses have become caves forever, thorns and a delight for wild donkeys, and pasture for flocks of sheep.
Until a spirit from on high is awakened over us, and the wilderness becomes like fruitful land, and the fruitful land is considered a forest.
Justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will be bestowed in Carmel.
The work of righteousness will be peace, and the service of righteousness will be quietness and confidence forever and ever.
My people will live in a peaceful dwelling, in a home of confidence and a resting place of confidence.
Hail will come down on the forest, and the city will be brought low like a plain.
Blessed are you who sow beside every water, where the ox and the donkey tread.

Woe to you who plunder! You will not plunder, and the treacherous one will not deal treacherously with you. When you wish to plunder, you will be plundered; when you wish to deal treacherously, you will be dealt with treacherously.
Lord, have mercy on us, for our hope is in you. Be our helper in the morning and our deliverer in a time of distress.
At the sound of your terror the peoples fled, and at your exaltation the nations scattered.
Now your plunder will be gathered like the gathering of caterpillars, like a swarm of locusts gathered together.
The Lord, who dwells on high, is exalted, and he has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
Your time will be faithfulness, and your salvation will be in shelter. Wisdom and knowledge—the fear of the Lord is his treasure.
If he appears to them, they will wail loudly, and the messengers of peace will weep bitterly.
The paths are deserted, and travelers have ceased passing along the road. The covenant has been broken, the cities have been despised, and people have been disregarded.
The earth lamented and sat in mourning. Lebanon was humiliated and ashamed. Sharon became like a desert plain; Bashan and Carmel were laid waste.
“Now I will rise,” says the Lord. “Now I will be exalted, and now I will be lifted up.
You will conceive thorns and give birth to stubble. Through your breath, fire will consume you.
The peoples will be burned like lime; like thorns gathered together, they will burn in the fire.
You who are far away, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge my might.”
The sinners in Zion were terrified, and trembling seized the godless: Who among us can dwell with consuming fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting burning?

The one who walks in righteousness and speaks honestly, who hates deceit and oppression, who shakes his hand free of taking a bribe, who closes his ears so as not to hear and shuts his eyes so as not to see evil.
He will dwell on high, and his dwelling will be in a rocky stronghold. His bread will be supplied, and his water will be assured.
Your eyes will see the king in his beauty in distant lands.
Your heart will learn fear: “Where is the scribe? Where is the one who weighs? Where is the one who counts the towers?”
He will not look upon the mighty people, the people whose speech is difficult to understand, whose tongue stammers and cannot be understood.
Look at Zion, the city of our festivals. Your eyes will gaze on Jerusalem, a prosperous dwelling, a tent that does not move, whose stakes will never be pulled up and whose ropes will never be broken.

For the Lord is a glorious name for us. He will be for us a bright place, brightness and room to spread our hands, where a ruler's dominion will not reign, and no mighty one who is found will pass through it.
For the Lord is the judge, the Lord is the one who declares, the Lord is our king, and he is our savior.
Your ropes came loose and were not secured, and your masts bent down and did not spread a sail, until they divided the plunder and a multitude of lame people took captives.
No inhabitant will say, “I am sick.” The people living in it have received sin [?], a place of judgment.
Come near to hear, you peoples, and listen, you nations. Let the earth and everything in it hear, the world and all its inhabitants.
For the Lord's anger is against all the nations, and his fury against all their armies, to destroy them and hand them over to slaughter.
Their slain will be thrown out, the stench of their corpses will rise, and the mountains will melt from their blood.
All the forces of heaven will melt away, and the heavens will be rolled up like a scroll. All their forces will fall like leaves falling from a vine, and like an unripe fig from a fig tree.
For my sword will drink its fill in heaven. Look, it will come down upon the Edomites, upon the people condemned in judgment.

The Lord’s sword is full of blood. It is coated with blood and with the fat of fattened animals and goats, and with the fat of rams’ kidneys. For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
Wild oxen will fall with them, and bulls with oxen. The land will be drenched with their blood, and the dust will be coated with their fat.
For the LORD has a day of vengeance and a year of repayment for the judge of Zion.
Her streams will turn into pitch, and her dust into sulfur; her land will become burning pitch.
It will not be extinguished night or day, and its smoke will rise forever. It will lie desolate from generation to generation, and no one will ever pass through it.
Pelicans and hedgehogs will possess it, and owls and ravens will live in it. A measuring line of desolation will be stretched over it.
There will be no joy there, nor will they proclaim a kingdom, and all her nobles will come to destruction.
Thorns will grow in its courtyards, and nettles and thistles in its stronghold. It will become a home for jackals and a grazing place for ostriches.
Spirits will meet apparitions there, and a demon will call to its companion. There Lilith has rested and found herself a resting place.
There the hedgehog has nested, given birth, burrowed, and hatched its young under its shade. There kites have gathered, each beside another.
Search in the Lord’s book and read: not one of them is missing, and none needs to search for another. For he himself gave the command with his mouth, and his Spirit gathered them.
He cast lots for them, and his hand divided the measured portions among them, so that they will possess it forever and live in it from generation to generation.
The thirsty wilderness will rejoice, and the plain will exult and blossom like a lily.

It will rejoice joyfully and with praise. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, and the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the Lord and the splendor of our God. Exhortation and encouragement for the weak: the Savior is coming and will save them.
Be strengthened, weak hands, and be made firm, trembling knees.
Say to the fainthearted, “Be strong and do not be afraid. Look, your God, the avenger, is coming. God the Savior is coming and will save you.”
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be opened.
Then the lame person will leap like a deer, and the stammerer’s tongue will be loosened, because waters have burst forth in the wilderness and streams in the plain.
There will be pools in the desolate place and springs of water in the thirsty land. Grass, reeds, and rushes will grow in the jackals’ dwelling.
There will be a path there, and it will be called the Holy Way. No uncleanness will pass along it, and there will be no road in it. Fools will not go astray there.
No lion will be there, and dangerous animals will not come up onto it or be found there. The redeemed will walk there.
The Lord’s redeemed will return and enter Zion with praise. Everlasting joy will be upon their heads. They will attain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee.
In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah king of Judah, Sennacherib king of Assyria marched against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem with a large army. He stood by the conduit of the upper pool, on the road to the fuller’s field.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to him.
Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah: This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this confidence on which you rely?
You say that you have words on your lips, strategy, and strength for war. Now, whom have you relied on, that you have rebelled against me?

Look, you have relied on the support of a broken reed—on Egypt—which enters a person’s hand and pierces it when he leans on it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is like for everyone who relies on him.
If you tell me, ‘We rely on the Lord our God,’ what has Hezekiah gained by removing the high places and altars and telling Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship before one altar’?
Now make a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you have riders to mount them.
How can you turn back even one of my master’s least servants, when you have relied on Egypt to give you chariots and horsemen?
Now, have I come up against this land to destroy it without the LORD? The LORD himself told me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, ‘Speak to your servants in Aramaic, because we understand it. Do not speak to us in Judean in front of the people standing on the wall.’

The Rabshakeh said to them, ‘My master did not send me to you and your master to say these things, but to the men sitting on the wall, so that they will not eat their own excrement and drink their own urine along with you.’
Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in Judean, saying, ‘Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!’
This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, because he cannot rescue you.
‘Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD by saying, “The LORD will certainly rescue us, and this city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.”’

‘Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you may eat from his own vines and his own fig trees and drink water from his own well,
until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and oil, a land of olive trees and vineyards.’
‘Do not let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, “The LORD will rescue us.” Have the gods of the nations rescued their respective lands from the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they rescue Samaria from my hands?
Which of all the gods of these lands has rescued his land from my hands, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from my hands?’
They remained silent, and no one answered him, because the king had commanded, “Do not answer him.”
Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and reported the Rabshakeh’s words to him.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and entered the house of the Lord.
He sent Eliakim, the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, dressed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, ‘This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and wrath, for the labor pains for the children have come, but the woman giving birth has no strength.

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master, the king of Assyria, sent to insult the living God, and will rebuke him for the words that the LORD your God has heard. So offer supplication and pray for the remnant that is left.’
The servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, ‘Tell your master this: This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the messengers of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.’
“Look, I will put a spirit upon him, and he will hear a report and return to his own land. I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.”
The Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had left Lachish.
He heard about Tirhakah, king of Cush, and he went out to fight him. When he heard, he sent messengers to Hezekiah.
‘Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you when you say, “Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.”
Look, you have heard everything the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, destroying them. Will you be rescued?
Did their gods rescue the nations my ancestors destroyed—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?’
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, and those of Hena and Ivvah?”
Hezekiah received the letters from the messengers and read them. He went up to the house of the LORD, and Hezekiah spread them out before the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed before the Lord and said:
‘LORD Almighty, God of Israel, enthroned upon the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.
Bend your ear, LORD, and hear. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib, which he sent to insult the living God.
Truly, Lord, the kings of Assyria have devastated all the lands and their own land.
They burned their gods in the fire, because they were not gods but the work of human hands, made of wood, silver, and stone, and they destroyed them.
Now, LORD our God, save us from his hands, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are God.’
Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah, saying, ‘This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: I have heard everything you prayed before me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria.
This is the word that the LORD has spoken against him: The virgin daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
Whom have you insulted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!

Through your messengers you have insulted the LORD and said, “With my many chariots I will climb the mountain heights and the slopes of Lebanon. I will cut down its tall cedars and its choicest cypresses, and I will enter the farthest heights of the forest of Carmel.”
I will dig and drink water, and with the hooves of my horses I will dry up all the mighty rivers.”
Have you not heard that I did this long ago and prepared it in ancient days? Now I have brought it about, so that it would become a ruin and a wasteland, like the fortified cities.

Their inhabitants lost their strength; they were shattered and ashamed. They became like grass in the field, like tender green shoots, like grain growing on a rooftop, and like blighted grain before it grows tall.
I know where you sit, when you come in and when you go out, and how you have acted insolently before me.

Because you have acted arrogantly before me, and your blasphemy has reached my ears, I will put a ring in your nose and a bridle between your lips, and I will turn you back along the road by which you came.

This will be a sign for you: this year you will eat what grows on its own, and in the second year what springs up from that. In the third year you will sow and reap, plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
The remnant of the house of Judah who survive will again be like a root that reaches downward and bears fruit upward.
For a remnant will come out of Jerusalem and escape from Mount Zion. The zeal of the mighty LORD will do this.
Therefore this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: “He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow there. He will not confront it with shields or lay ambushes against it.”
Instead, he will return along the road by which he came, and he will not enter this city,’ says the Lord.
‘I will defend this city and save it for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.’”
The angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. When people rose early in the morning, there they all were—dead bodies.
Sennacherib departed and returned home, and he lived in Nineveh.

While he was worshiping in the temple of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with the sword. They fled to the land of the people of Corduene, and his son Esarhaddon became king in his place.

In those days Hezekiah became deathly ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, “This is what the LORD says: Put your household affairs in order, because you are going to die; you will not live.”
Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall, and Hezekiah prayed before the Lord.
He said, “Please, LORD, remember that I have walked before you faithfully and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the Lord came to Isaiah, saying:
Go and tell Hezekiah king of Judah, “This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Look, I am adding fifteen years to your life.”
I will rescue you and this city from the hands of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.
This will be your sign from the Lord that the Lord will do what he has said:
“Look, I will turn back by ten steps the shadow that the sun has cast down on the steps of your father Ahaz.” And the sun went back ten steps along the steps it had descended.
The writing of Hezekiah, king of Judah, when he became sick and recovered from his illness.
I said, “In the middle of my days I am going through the gate of Sheol; I have left behind the rest of my years.”
I said, “I will not see the Lord in the land of the living. I will no longer see human beings among those who dwell in the dust.”
My dwelling has been pulled up and taken away from me like a shepherd’s tent. My life has been folded up like [?], like a web about to be cut off. From day until night you have brought me to an end.
I chirped like a chirping swallow and moaned like a dove. I lifted my eyes on high: “LORD, rescue me and heal me.”
What can I say? He spoke to me, and he passed on and drove away all my sleep because of the bitterness of my soul.
Lord, people live by these things; because of these things my spirit lives. Heal me and let me live.
Look, instead of peace I had bitter suffering. But you wanted my life not to waste away in destruction, for you have thrown all my sins behind your back.
For Sheol will not thank you, nor will death praise you. Those who go down to the pit will not hope for your faithfulness.
Instead, the living will thank you, as I do today, and a father will make your faithfulness known to his children.
The Lord will save us, and we will sing his praises all the days of our lives in the house of the Lord.
Isaiah said, “Let them take a cake of figs and put it on the boil, and he will recover.”
Hezekiah said, “What is the sign that I will go up to the house of the Lord?”
At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and gifts to Hezekiah, because he had heard that Hezekiah had been ill, had regained his strength, and had recovered.

Hezekiah was pleased with them and showed them his treasury—the silver, gold, spices, and fine oil—as well as his entire armory and everything found in his treasuries. Hezekiah left nothing in his palace or anywhere in his dominion that he did not show them.
The prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and said to him, “What did these men say to you, and where did they come from?” Hezekiah said, “They came to me from a distant land, Babylon.”
He said, “What have they seen in your palace?” Hezekiah said, “They have seen everything in my palace. I left nothing in my palace that I did not show them.”
Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the Lord Almighty:

“Look, days are coming when everything in your palace will be taken away, and the treasure your ancestors have stored up until this day will go to Babylon. Nothing will be left to you,” says the LORD.
Some of your sons who come from you, whom you will father, will be taken away and become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the Lord that you have spoken is good. Let there be peace and truth in my days.”
“Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God.

Speak tenderly to Jerusalem and proclaim to her that her term of service is complete, that she has made satisfaction for her sin, and that she has received from the LORD’s hand double for all her sins.
A voice cries in the wilderness: “Prepare a road for the Lord, and make straight paths for our God in the plain.
All the valleys will be filled, and all the mountains and hills will be lowered. Rough ground will become smooth, and difficult terrain a plain.
The glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all flesh will see it together, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.”
A voice says, “Cry out!” And he said, “What shall I cry out?” “All flesh is grass, and all its beauty is like the blossom of the field.
The grass has dried up and the blossom has withered, because the breath of the Lord has blown upon it. Such is the grass of this people.
The grass dries up and the blossom withers, but the word of our God stands forever.”
Go up onto the high mountains, Zion, bearer of good news. Raise your voice with strength, Jerusalem, bearer of good news. Raise it and do not be afraid. Say to the towns of Judah, “Here is your God!”
Look, the Lord God comes with might, and his arm is powerful. Look, his reward is with him, and his work is before him.
Like a shepherd who tends his flock, he gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them close to his chest, and he provides for those nursing their young.
Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, measured the heavens with his span, measured the earth’s dust in his measure, and weighed the mountains with weights and the hills in scales?
Who has directed the Spirit of the Lord, or who has been his counselor?
Whom did he consult, who taught him, made him understand the way of justice, taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?
Look, the nations are like a drop from a bucket and like a speck on the scales, and the islands are thrown about like ashes.
He does not consider Lebanon sufficient for burning, nor its animals sufficient for a burnt offering.
All the nations are considered nothing by him; he considers them destruction and desolation.
To whom have you compared God, and to what likeness have you likened him?
Is it an image that a carpenter has made, which a metalworker has overlaid with gold, and refined silver
He fastens choice wood in it [?], wood that does not rot, and chooses a carpenter, who carves it with his skill and sets up an image that will not move.
Have you not heard? Have you not known? Has it not been told to you from the beginning? Have you not understood the foundations of the earth?
And the one who sits above the circle of the earth, whose inhabitants are like grasshoppers, who stretches out the heavens like a dome and spreads them out like a tent to live in.
He makes rulers nothing and the judges of the earth as though they did not exist.
They will not plant or sow or put down roots in the earth. He will blow on them, and they will wither, and a whirlwind will carry them away like stubble.
“To whom have you compared me, that I should be his equal?” says the Holy One.
Lift your eyes on high and see who created these, who brings out their hosts by number and calls them all by name. Because of his great majesty and the strength of his might, not one goes astray.
Why do you speak, Jacob, and say, Israel, “My ways are hidden from the LORD, and my case is passed over by my God”?
Have you not known? Have you not heard that the LORD is God forever, the one who created the ends of the earth? He does not grow weary or tired, and his understanding cannot be fathomed.
He gives strength to the weary and increases the strength of those suffering pain.
Young men will grow weary and become tired, and warriors will surely stumble.
Those who hope in the LORD will renew their strength and grow wings like a dove’s. They will run and not grow tired; they will walk and not grow weary.
Be silent, islands, and let the nations renew their strength. Let them approach and then speak; let them come forward together for judgment.

Who stirred up righteousness from the east and called it to his feet? Nations will be delivered before him, and kings will be shattered. He will make his sword like dust, and his bow like falling [?].
He will pursue them and make peace, and he will not enter a road on foot.
Who prepared and accomplished this? The one who called the generations from the beginning. I, I am the LORD, the first, and I, I am the last.
The islands saw me and were afraid. The ends of the earth were afraid; they drew near and came.
Each helps his companion and says to his brother, “Be strong!”
The carpenter encourages the metalworker, who fashions it with a hammer and works on it. He says of the joint, “It is good,” and they fasten it with nails so that it will not move.
But now, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham, my friend,
You whom I strengthened from the ends of the earth and called from its heights, to whom I said, “You are my servant; I chose you and did not reject you.”
Do not be afraid, because I am with you. Do not be alarmed, because I am your God. I strengthened you, helped you, and supported you with my righteous right hand.
Those who hate you will be ashamed and disgraced. The men who quarrel with you will become nothing and perish.
You will look for the men who quarrel with you but will not find them. The men who fight against you will become as though they did not exist.
For I am the LORD your God, who strengthens your right hand. I have said to you, “Do not be afraid; I am your helper.”
Do not be afraid, you worm Jacob, you small company of Israel. I am your helper, says the LORD, and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
Look, I have made you like a new threshing roller that crushes and pulverizes. You will thresh mountains and crush them, and you will make the hills like chaff.
You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and a whirlwind will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD and boast in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and afflicted seek water, but there is none, and their tongues are dry with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.
I will open rivers in the mountains and springs in the valleys. I will turn the wilderness into pools of water and the thirsty land into springs of water.
I will plant cedars, boxwood, myrtle, and olive trees in the wilderness. I will place splendid cypresses together in the valley.
So that they may see and know, recognize and understand together that the hand of the Lord has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
Present your cases, says the Lord; present your arguments, says the King of Jacob.
Let them come forward and show what is to come. Tell us what the former things were, so that we may take them to heart and know their outcome. Or let us hear of things to come.
Show us the signs that are to come, so that we may know that you are gods. Do good or do evil, so that we may speak and see together.
Look, you are nothing, and your works come from destruction. Choosing you is an abomination.
I have stirred up someone from the north to come from the rising of the sun, and he will call on my name. Rulers will come and be trampled like clay that a potter treads.
Who declared this from the beginning, so that we might know and say, “He is right”? There is no one who declares it, no one who announces it, and no one who hears your words.
These are the beginnings of Zion, and I will give Jerusalem a messenger of good news.
I looked, but there was no one who considered these things, whom I could question and who could give me an answer.
Look, they are all nothing, and their works are empty. Their works are an empty wind.
Look, I have upheld my servant, and my soul delights in my chosen one. I have put my Spirit upon him, so that he may bring forth justice to the nations.
He will not shout or quarrel, and his voice will not be heard in the street.
He will not break a damaged reed or extinguish a flickering lamp. He will bring forth justice in truth.
He will not go out or flicker until he establishes justice on earth, and the islands will wait for his law.

This is what the Lord God says, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and everything in it, who gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those who walk on it:
I, the Lord, have called you in righteousness. I have taken you by the hand and strengthened you. I have given you as a covenant for the people and a light for the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, to bring the prisoner out of confinement, and those who sit in darkness out of prison.
I am the Lord, and that is my name. I will not give my glory to another, nor my praise to carved idols.
I am declaring new things, and look, the former things have come. Before they sprouted, I made them known to you.
The Song of Isaiah. Sing a new song to the Lord, his praise from the ends of the earth, you who go down to the sea and all that fills it, the islands and those who live in them.
Let the wilderness and its villages rejoice, and let Kedar become meadows. Let those who live among the rocks sing praise, and let them shout from the mountaintops.
Let them give praise to the Lord and proclaim his praises in the islands.
The Lord will go out like a mighty warrior. Like a man of war, he will stir up his zeal. He will shout, show his might, and kill his enemies.
I have been silent for a long time; I will keep silent. I have held back. Like a woman in labor, I will gasp and lay waste all at once.
I will devastate mountains and hills and dry up all their strength. I will turn rivers into islands and dry up pools.

I will lead the blind along a road they do not know, and guide them along paths they have not known. I will turn darkness into light before them and level the rough ground. These are the things I have done, and I have not abandoned them.
Those who trust in carved idols and say to cast images, “You are our gods,” will turn back and be utterly ashamed.
Listen, you deaf! Look carefully and see, you blind!
Who is blind but my servant, or deaf like my messenger whom I send? Who is blind like the ruler, and blind like the servant of the Lord?
I have looked often, but you do not pay attention; I have opened ears, but you do not listen.
For the sake of his righteousness, the LORD desired to make the law great and glorious.

But this is a plundered and trampled people. They are all trapped by raiding bands [?] and hidden away in prisons. They have become plunder, with no one to rescue them, and a thing to be trampled, with no one to bring them back.
Who among you will hear this, pay attention, and listen for what is to come?
Who gave Jacob over to be trampled and Israel to be plundered? Was it not the Lord, against whom we sinned, whose ways we would not walk in, and whose law we did not obey?
He poured out on them his furious anger and the violence of war. It burned them on every side, but they did not understand. Fire blazed among them, but they did not take it to heart.
But now this is what the Lord says, who created you, Jacob, and formed you, Israel: Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name; you are mine.
If you pass through the sea, I am with you, and the rivers will not sweep you away. If you walk through fire, you will not be scorched, and the flame will not burn you.
For I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I have given Egypt in exchange for you, and Cush and Sheba on your behalf.
Because you are precious in my eyes, you have been honored, and I have loved you. I have given people in exchange for you and nations in exchange for your life.
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west.
I will say to the north, “Give them up,” and to the south, “Do not hold them back. Bring my sons from far away and my daughters from the ends of the earth.”
Everyone who is called by my name—I created him for my glory; I formed him and made him.”
Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and those who have ears but are deaf.

Let all the nations gather together, and let the peoples assemble. Who among you can declare this and tell us the former things? Let them bring their witnesses to prove themselves right, so that people may hear and say, “It is true.”

“You are my witnesses,” says the Lord, “and my servants whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he. Before me no god was created, and after me there will be none.”
I, I am the LORD, and there is no other besides me.
“I declared, saved, and made it known, and there is no foreign god among you. You are my witnesses,” says the Lord, “and I am God.”
Even from the first day, I am he. No one can escape from my hands, and who can reverse what I do?”
This is what the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says: “For your sake I sent to Babylon and brought all the fugitives and the Chaldeans who boast about their ships.”
I am the LORD, your Holy One, who created Israel, your King.”
This is what the LORD says, who makes a way through the sea and a path through mighty waters,
He brings out chariots and horses and a mighty army. Together they will lie down and not rise; they will be extinguished like a flickering lamp.
Do not remember the former things or dwell on the things of old.
“Look, I am doing something new! Now it will spring up, and you will recognize it. I will make a road in the wilderness and rivers in the desert.”
“The wild animals will praise me, the jackals and the ostriches, because I have provided water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert for my chosen people to drink.”
This people whom I have chosen for myself will drink.
It was not you who called on me, Jacob, but I who called you, Israel.
“You have not brought me lambs for your burnt offerings, nor honored me with your sacrifices. I have not enslaved you with offerings or wearied you with frankincense.”
“You have not bought fragrant cane for me with silver, nor satisfied me with the fat of your sacrifices. Instead, you have enslaved me with your sins and wearied me with your wrongdoing.”
I, I am the one who wipes away your wrongdoing for my own sake, and I will no longer remember your sins.
Remind me; let us argue our case together. State your case, so that you may be justified.
Your first father sinned, and your rulers acted wickedly against me.
Your leaders defiled the sanctuary. I handed Jacob over to destruction and Israel to disgrace.
Now listen to me, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
This is what the Lord says, who made you, formed you in the womb, and helped you: “Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen.”
“For I will give water in the thirsty land and streams on the dry ground. I will pour out my Spirit on your offspring and my blessings on your children.”
They will spring up among the grass, like willows beside the water.
One will say, “I belong to the Lord,” and another will call himself by the name of Jacob. Another will write on his hand, “The Lord’s,” and take the name of Israel.
This is what the Lord, the King of Israel and its Redeemer, whose name is the Lord Almighty, says: “I am the first, and I am the last, and there is no God besides me.”
Who is like me? Let him proclaim it, prepare, and declare what has happened since I established a people forever. Let them declare the signs that are coming.
“Do not be afraid or alarmed. Did I not make you hear and tell you long ago? You are my witnesses that there is no God besides me, and there is no mighty one whom I do not know.”

All the craftsmen who make idols are worthless, and there is no benefit in the things they have desired to make. The craftsmen who made them testify that they do not see, hear, or know. Because of this they will be ashamed.
Those who make gods and carve cast images in which there is no benefit.
Look, all their makers are craftsmen from among human beings. Let them all gather and stand up; together they will be ashamed and disgraced.
The craftsman who sharpens iron smooths it with a file, carves it with a chisel, and works it with the strength of his arm. He becomes hungry and thirsty, drinks no water, and grows faint.
The carpenter selects wood and measures it, joins it with glue, carves it, and makes it in the likeness of a man, with human beauty, and sets it up in a house.
The wood that was cut from the forest, which grew through the rain.
It serves people as fuel. They take some of it, warm themselves, and bake bread. They also make a god and worship it; they make a carved image and bow down to it.
They burn half of it in the fire, roast meat over its coals, and eat until they are full. They also warm themselves and say, “Ah, I am warm! I have seen the fire!”
With the rest they made a carved god, bowed down to it, prayed to it, and said, “Save us, for you are our god!”
They did not know or understand, because the sight of their eyes and the understanding of their hearts were obscured.

They do not take it to heart, nor do they know or consider and say that they have burned half of it in the fire, baked bread over its coals, roasted meat and eaten it, and made the rest into a wooden idol for themselves and bowed down to it.
Their heart feeds on ashes and leads them astray. They wander astray and do not save themselves, nor do they say, “Our right hand has made a falsehood.”
“Remember these things, Jacob, and Israel, for you are my servant. I formed you to be my servant. From now on, Israel, do not forget me.”
I have swept away your wrongdoing like mist and your sins like a cloud. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.

Praise, heavens, for the Lord has acted! Shout for joy, foundations of the earth! Break into joyful praise, mountains, and the forest and every tree in it, for the Lord has redeemed Jacob and has been glorified in Israel.

This is what the Lord says, who redeemed you, formed you in the womb, and helped you: “I am the Lord, who made everything, who stretched out the heavens alone and spread out the earth by myself and for myself.”
“I frustrate the signs of soothsayers and make fools of their diviners. I turn the wise back and make their knowledge foolish.”

He confirms the word of his servant and fulfills the purpose of his messengers. He says of Jerusalem, “It will be inhabited,” and of the towns of Judah, “They will be rebuilt, and I will restore her ruins.”
I say to the deep, ‘Dry up! I will dry up your rivers.’
I say of Cyrus, ‘He is my shepherd, and he will fulfill all my wishes,’ saying of Jerusalem, ‘It will be rebuilt,’ and, ‘The temple will be completed.’”

This is what the Lord says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped so that nations will be subjected before him: “I will unfasten the belts of kings, opening doors before him so that the gates will not be shut.”
I will go before you and level the heights. I will break bronze doors and cut through iron bars.
I will give you treasures in darkness and hidden stores, so that you may know that I am the Lord, who called you by your name, the God of Israel.
For the sake of my servant Jacob and Israel my chosen one, I called you by your name and gave you a title, though you did not know me.
I am the Lord, and there is no other. Apart from me there is no God. I strengthened you, though you did not know me,
so that people may know, from the rising of the sun to its setting, that there is none besides me. I am the Lord, and there is no other.
I form light and create darkness; I make peace and create calamity. I am the Lord, who has done all these things.
Rejoice, heavens above, and let the clouds sprinkle righteousness. Let the earth open, let salvation abound, and let righteousness spring up together with it. I am the Lord, who created these things.
Woe to anyone who disputes with his maker—a potsherd among the potsherds of the earth! Does clay say to the potter, “What are you making?” and, “I was not the work of your hands”?
Woe to anyone who says to a father, ‘What are you fathering?’ or to a woman, ‘What have you conceived?’”
This is what the Lord says, the Holy One of Israel and its maker, whose name is the Mighty Lord: “Ask me for signs concerning my children, and give me commands concerning the work of my hands.”
I made the earth and humanity upon it. With my own hands I stretched out the heavens, and I commanded all their host.
I have stirred him up in righteousness, and I will make all his paths smooth. He will rebuild my city and send my exiles home, without payment or a bribe, says the Mighty Lord.

This is what the Lord says: “The wealth earned by Egypt’s labor, the merchants of Cush and Sheba, men of stature, will come over to you and belong to you. They will follow you and come over in chains. They will bow down to you and pray to you, saying, ‘God is in you, and there is no other god.’”
Truly, you are hidden, the God of Israel and its Savior.
They were all ashamed and disgraced together, those who walk in disgrace and carve idols.
Israel’s salvation is in the Lord, the eternal Savior. You will never be ashamed or disgraced, forever and ever.

For this is what the Lord says, who created the heavens—he is God—who formed the earth and made it, who established it: He did not create it in vain, but so that his creation might live in it. “I am the Lord, and there is no other.”
I did not speak in secret, in a place in a dark land. Nor did I say to Jacob’s descendants, “Seek me in vain.” I am the Lord, who speaks righteousness and declares what is right.
Gather and come; draw near together, you who escape from the nations. Those who carry carved wood and pray to a god who cannot save have no understanding.

Declare it and present your case; take counsel together. Who announced this long ago, from the beginning? I am the Lord, and there is no other god besides me, a righteous God and a Savior; there is none besides me.
“Draw near to me, all the ends of the earth, so that you may be saved, for I am the Lord, and there is no other.
I have sworn by myself; a word of righteousness has gone out from my mouth and will not return: Every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will swear by me.
They will say, “Righteousness is in the Lord,” and the mighty will go to him. All who are hostile to you will be ashamed.
“In me all Israel’s descendants will boast and be justified.”
Bel has fallen, and Nebo has been overturned. Their carved idols have become numerous loads for animals and hungry livestock.
They toppled and fell together. They could not rescue their loads, and they themselves went into captivity.
“Listen to me, house of Jacob and all the remnant of Israel, who are carried in the belly and carried in the womb.
Even to old age I am he, and even in advanced age I will carry you. I have made you, and I will bear you; I will carry you and rescue you.
To whom have you likened me and compared me?
To one who is carried. They take gold out of their purses and weigh silver on a scale. They hire a metalworker and make a god, bow down to it, and even pray to it.
They lift it onto their shoulders, carry it along, and set it in its place. It cannot rise from its place. They even pray to it, but it does not answer them or save them from their troubles.
Remember these things and consider them; take your wrongdoings to heart.
“Remember the former things from long ago, for I am God, and there is no other god; there is none like me.
I declare the end from the beginning, and from long ago things that have not yet happened. I say, “I will establish my purpose and do everything I desire.”
I call a bird from the east, and from a distant land a man to carry out my purpose. I have spoken, and I will also bring it about. I have formed it, and I will also do it.
“Listen to me, you stubborn-hearted people, far from righteousness.
My righteousness is close to arriving, and my salvation will not be delayed. I will give salvation in Zion and my glory to Israel.
Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground, daughter of the Chaldeans; there is no throne. For they will no longer call you delicate and pampered.
“Take the millstones and grind flour. Remove your veil, cut off your white garments, uncover your legs, and cross the rivers.
“Your nakedness will be uncovered, and your shame will be seen. I will take vengeance on you, and I will not meet you as a man.”
Our Redeemer—the Lord Almighty is his name—is the Holy One of Israel.
Sit in [?]; enter the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, for they will no longer call you the mighty lady of kingdoms.
I was angry with my people because they defiled my inheritance, and I handed them over to you. You showed them no mercy, and you made your yoke very heavy on the elderly.
You said, “I will be mighty forever.” You did not take these things to heart or consider the outcome.
Now hear these things, you pampered woman who sits undisturbed and says in her heart, “I am, and there is no other. I will not sit as a widow or know the loss of children.”
Both these blows will come upon you in a single day: the loss of children and widowhood. They will come upon you suddenly, despite your many sorceries and your many magicians.
You trusted in your wickedness and said, “No one sees me.” Your wisdom and your knowledge led you astray, and you said in your heart, “I am, and there is no one else.”
Evil will come upon you in the morning, and you will not know it. Disaster will fall upon you, and you will not be able to remove it. Turmoil will come upon you suddenly, without your knowing.
Stand now with your magicians and your many spells, over which you have labored from your youth. Perhaps you will be able to benefit; perhaps you will grow strong.
You have worn yourself out with your many plans. Let the Chaldeans who gaze at the heavens and the stars stand up and save you, those who tell you each month what is coming upon you.
Look, they have become like stubble that fire has burned, and they will not rescue themselves from the power of the flame. There are no coals for their fire, nor any glow to sit before.
This is what your merchants have become to you, those over whom you have labored from your youth. Each has wandered off in his own direction, and there is no one to save you.

Hear these things, house of Jacob, who are called by the name of Israel and have come from the [?] of Judah, who swear by the name of the Lord and invoke the God of Israel, but not in truth or righteousness.
For they are named after the holy city and rely on the God of Israel; the Lord Almighty is his name.
I declared the former things from the beginning. They came from my mouth, and I made them known. Suddenly I act, and they come to pass.
I know that you are stubborn, that your neck is an iron sinew and your forehead is bronze.
I declared it to you long ago, and before it happened I made it known to you, so that you would not say, “My idols did it; my carved images and my cast images saved me.”
You have heard and seen all these things. Will you not declare them? I have made new things known to you from now on, things kept hidden that you did not know.
They are being created now, not long ago. Before today you had not heard them, so that you could not say, “I know them.”
You have not heard, nor do you know them; your ears were not opened long ago. I know that you are utterly deceitful, and you were called a wrongdoer from the womb.
For the sake of my name I will delay my anger, and I will preserve my praise for you and will not destroy you.
Look, I have refined you, but not with silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of poverty.
For my own sake I will act, so that I am not defiled. I will not give my glory to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, and Israel, whom I called. I am the first, and I am the last.
My hand established the foundations of the earth, and my right hand spread out the heavens. I call to them, and they stand together.
Gather, all of you, and listen. Who among you declares these things? The Lord desires to carry out his will against Babylon and against the offspring of the Chaldeans.
I have spoken, and I have also called. I have brought her and made her way successful.
Come near me and hear this: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret. From the time it happened, I was there. And now the Lord God has sent me, and his Spirit.
This is what the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says: “I am the Lord your God. I teach you so that you do not act unjustly, and I show you the way you should go.”
If only you had listened to my commandments! Your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your descendants would have been like the sand, and the offspring of your body like its pebbles. His name would not be cut off or perish from before me.
Go out from Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! Declare this with a voice of praise and make it heard. Send it out to the ends of the earth and say, “The Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob.”
He led them through desolate places and made water flow for them from the flint. He split the rock, and water flowed out.
“There is no peace for the wicked,” says the Lord.
Be silent, islands, and listen, nations far away. The Lord called me from the womb; from my mother’s womb he mentioned my name.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword and hid me in the shadow of his hand. He made me like a choice arrow and concealed me in his quiver.
He said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.”
I did not say to the descendants of Jacob, “I have labored in vain and spent my strength for nothing.” Surely my cause is before the Lord, and my work before my God.
Now this is what the Lord says, who formed me in the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him and gather Israel: I was honored before the Lord, and my God became my strength.

He said, “It is too small a thing for you to be my servant, to raise up the tribe of Jacob and bring back the offspring of Israel. I have made you a light to the nations, so that you may be my salvation to the ends of the earth.”

This is what the Lord, the Holy One of Israel and its Redeemer, says to the one whose life is despised, who is despised by the people and by the servants of rulers: “Kings will see and rise, and rulers will bow down to him, because of the Lord, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who chose you.”

This is what the Lord says: “At a time of favor I answered you, and on a day of salvation I helped you. I formed you and made you a covenant for the people and a light to the nations, to restore the land and inherit the inheritance of the desolate places.”
And you will say to the prisoners, “Come out,” and to those shut in, “Show yourselves.” They will graze along the roads, and all the paths will be their pastures.
They will neither hunger nor thirst, and neither the heat nor the sun will harm them, because the one who has compassion on them will lead them and bring them to springs of water.
I will turn all the mountains into roads, and the paths will be raised up.
These will come from far away, and these from the north, and these from the sea and from the sea of Sinim.
Sing praise, heavens, and rejoice, earth! Break into joyful praise, mountains, because the Lord has comforted his people and had compassion on his afflicted ones.
But Zion said, “The Lord has abandoned me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”
Can a woman forget her infant and have no compassion on the son of her womb? Even if these women forget, I will not forget you.
Look, I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands, and your walls are always before me.
Soon your children [?]; those who tore you down and destroyed you will leave you.
Lift your eyes and look around you: they are all gathering and coming to you. As I live, says the Lord, you will wear them all like ornaments and adorn yourself with them like a bride.
For your ruins, your desolate places, and your devastated land will now be too crowded with inhabitants, and those who devoured you will flee.
The children of your bereavement will again say in your hearing, “This place is too cramped for us. Make room for us to live.”
You will say in your heart, “Who has borne me these children? Look, I was bereaved and desolate, exiled and driven away. Who raised these children? Look, I was left alone; where were these?”

This is what the Lord God says: Look, I am raising my hand to the nations, and I will raise a banner to the peoples. They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will be your foster fathers, and their noblewomen your nursing mothers. They will bow down to you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust of your feet. Then you will know that I am the Lord, and that those who wait for me will not be put to shame.
Can plunder be taken from a mighty warrior, or the captives of a powerful man be rescued?

For this is what the Lord says: What the warrior has carried off will be taken away, and the strong man’s captives will be rescued. I myself will judge those who contend with you, and I myself will save your children.

I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh, and they will become drunk on their own blood as on new wine. Then all humanity will know that I am the Lord, your Savior and your helper, the Mighty One of Jacob.

This is what the Lord says: Where is the certificate of divorce with which I divorced your mother? Or who is my creditor to whom I sold you? Look, you were sold because of your sins, and your mother was divorced because of your wrongdoing.

Why did I come and find no one, and call with no one answering? Has my hand been cut short and become powerless? Or do I have no strength to rescue? Look, with my rebuke I dry up the sea and make rivers like a desert. Their fish rot for lack of water and die.
I clothe the heavens in darkness and make sackcloth their covering.
The Lord God has given me a tongue trained in instruction, so that I may make a word known and explain it to the weary. Morning by morning he awakens me and gives me ears to hear instruction.
The Lord God has opened my ears, and I have not turned back or resisted.
I gave my body to blows and my cheeks to striking. I did not turn my face away from humiliation and spitting.
The Lord God has helped me; therefore I have not been put to shame. Therefore I have made my face like stone, and I know that I will not be put to shame.
For the one who vindicates me is near. Who will contend with me? Let us stand together. Who is my accuser? Let him approach me.
Look, the Lord God helps me. Who will condemn me? Look, they will all wear out like a garment, and the moth will eat them.
Who among you fears the Lord? Let him listen to the voice of his servant. Whoever walks in darkness and has no light, let him hope in the name of the Lord and be delivered by his God.
Look, all of you kindle fires and make flames blaze. Walk in the light of your fire and in the flame you have kindled. This has come to you from my hands: you will lie down in sorrow.
Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness and seek the Lord. Look at the mountain from which you were cut and the pit from which you were quarried.
Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah, who conceived you. He was only one when I called him, blessed him, and made him many.

For the Lord is rebuilding Zion and rebuilding all her ruins. He makes her wilderness like Eden and her plain like the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness will be heard within her, thanksgiving and the sound of singing.
Listen to me, peoples, and pay attention to me, nations, because instruction goes out from me, and my judgment is a light for the peoples.
My righteousness has drawn near, and my salvation has gone out. The peoples will be judged by my arm. The islands will wait for me and put their hope in my arm.

Lift your eyes to the heavens, and look also at the earth below, because the heavens will pass away like smoke, and the earth will wear out like a garment. Its inhabitants will become like it. But my salvation will last forever, and my righteousness will not pass away.
Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people who have my law in their hearts. Do not fear people’s insults, and do not be terrified by their abuse.
For the moth will eat them as it eats wool and clothing. But my righteousness will last forever, and my salvation through all generations.
Awake, awake, and put on the strength of the Lord’s arm! Awake as in the former days, as in the generations of long ago. You, you are the one who made the great division and destroyed the dragon.
You are the one who dried up the sea and the waters of the great deep, and made a road through the depths of the waters for the redeemed to cross.
The Lord’s redeemed will return and enter Zion with praise. Everlasting joy will be upon their heads. They will attain delight and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee.
“I, I am your comforter,” says the Lord. “Who are you that you fear a mortal person, a human being who withers like grass?

You have forgotten the Lord who made you, who stretched out the heavens and established the earth’s foundations. You have been afraid continually, every day, of the oppressor’s fury as he prepared to destroy. Where is the oppressor’s fury?
He was urging the mighty to destroy. They will not die and perish, nor will his bread run out.
I, I am the Lord your God, who rebukes the sea so that its waves grow quiet. The Mighty Lord is his name.
For I put my words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of my hands when I stretched out the heavens, established the earth’s foundations, and said to Zion, ‘You are my people.’”
Awake, awake, and rise, Jerusalem! You have drunk from the Lord’s hand the cup of his wrath; you have drunk and drained the cup of staggering.
Among all the sons she bore, there is no one to comfort her; among all the sons she raised, there is no one to take her by the hand.
These two things have happened to you—who will grieve over you?—plunder and destruction, famine and the sword. Who will comfort you?
Your sons are dazed and lie at the head of every street like a wilted beet. They are filled with the Lord’s wrath and your God’s rebuke.
Therefore hear these things, you who are afflicted and drunk, but not with wine.
This is what your Lord, the Lord, and your God, who will judge his people, says: “Look, I have taken the cup of staggering from your hands. You will never again drink the cup of my wrath.
I will put it into the hands of those who humiliate you, who said to you, ‘Bow down so that we may walk over you.’ You made your people like the ground, like a street for people to walk over.”
Awake, awake, Zion, and put on garments of praise, Jerusalem, the holy city! For the uncircumcised and the unclean will never enter you again.
Shake off the dust and rise; sit down, Jerusalem. Untie the yoke from your neck, captive daughter of Zion.
For this is what the Lord says: “You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed without money.”
For this is what the Lord God says: “My people first went down to Egypt to live there, and the Assyrian carried them away by force.
Now what have I here,” says the Lord, “since my people have been carried away for nothing? Their rulers howl,” says the Lord, “and continually, every day, they blaspheme my name.”
Therefore my people will know my name on that day, because I am the one speaking. Here I am.”
How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the one who announces peace, who brings good news and proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
Listen to your watchmen! They raise their voices and praise together, for they will see with their own eyes when the Lord restores Zion.
Rejoice and sing praise together, ruins of Jerusalem, for the Lord has comforted his people and redeemed Jerusalem.
The Lord has bared his holy arm in the sight of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
Depart, depart! Go out from there, and do not touch anything unclean. Come out from her midst and separate yourselves, you who carry the Lord’s vessels.
For you will not go out in haste or leave in flight, because the Lord goes before you, and the God of Israel gathers you together.
Look, my servant acts wisely. He will be raised up, lifted up, and greatly exalted.
Just as many will be astonished at him, so his appearance is marred beyond that of a man, and his form beyond that of human beings.
He cleanses many nations, and kings will shut their mouths because of him. For they have seen what they had not been told, and understood what they had not heard.
Who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
He grew up before him like a child, like a root out of dry ground. He had no beauty or splendor. We saw that he had no beauty, and we rejected him.
Despised and lowly among people, he was a man of pains, familiar with suffering. We turned our faces away from him, despised him, and considered him of no account.
Truly, he endured our sufferings and carried our pains, but we considered him stricken, struck by God, and humbled.
He was being killed because of our sins and humbled because of our wrongdoing. The punishment that brought us peace was upon him, and by his wounds we will be healed.
We have all strayed like sheep, and each of us has turned his own way. The Lord caused the sins of us all to fall upon him.
He came forward and was humbled, but he did not open his mouth. He was led like a lamb to slaughter, and like a ewe before its shearer he was silent and did not open his mouth.
He was led away from imprisonment and judgment. Who can describe his generation? For he was cut off from the land of the living, and some of the wicked among my people approached him.
A wicked man gave him his grave, and a rich man at his death, although he had done no wrong and there was no deceit in his mouth.
The Lord wished to humble him and make him suffer. Sin was laid upon his soul, so that he might see offspring and prolong his days, and the Lord’s will might prosper through him.
From the suffering of his soul he will see and be satisfied with knowledge. He, the servant of many, will vindicate the righteous, and he will bear their sins.

Therefore I will give him a share among the many, and he will divide the spoil with the mighty, because he poured out his life to death and was counted among the wicked. He bore the sins of many and interceded for the wicked.

Sing praise, barren woman who has not given birth! Break into joyful song and rejoice, you who have not been in labor! For the children of the deserted woman are more numerous than the children of the married woman, says the Lord.
Enlarge the space for your tents, and stretch out the curtains of your dwellings. Do not hold back! Lengthen your ropes and secure your stakes.
For you will spread out to the right and to the left. Your descendants will inherit nations and settle in desolate towns.

Do not be afraid, for you will not be ashamed. Do not be humiliated, for you will not be disgraced. For you will forget the shame of your youth and will no longer remember the reproach of your widowhood.
For your Lord has done this for you—the Lord Almighty is his name. Your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, will be called the God of the whole earth.
For the Lord has called you like a wife abandoned and distressed in spirit, like a wife married in youth who is abandoned, says your God.
In a little anger I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you.
In great anger I turned my face away from you, but with everlasting compassion I have had mercy on you, says the Lord your Redeemer.
This is like the days of Noah to me: just as I swore that the waters of Noah would never again pass over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.
For the mountains will be brought low and the hills will sink down, but my kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace with you will not pass away, says the compassionate Lord.
You who are humbled and storm-tossed, who have not been comforted: look, I am making your stones of beryl, and I will lay your foundations with sapphire stones.
I will build your walls with jasper stones, your gates with crystal stones, and your boundaries with choice stones.
All your children will learn to know me, and great will be the peace of your children.
You will be established in righteousness. Keep far from oppression, for you will not be afraid, and from destruction, for it will not come near you.
All who turn away from my hands will come to you, and you will be a place of refuge for your inhabitants.
Look, I created the craftsman who blows the bellows into the fire and finishes a tool for his work, and I created the destroyer to destroy.

No weapon made against you will succeed, and you will condemn every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the inheritance of the Lord’s servants, and their vindication comes from me, says the Lord.
Ho, all who are thirsty, go to the water! You who have no money, go, buy provisions and eat—wine and milk without money and without cost!
Why do you weigh out money for what is not bread, and spend your labor on what does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and you will eat good things, and your soul will delight in rich food.
Incline your ears and come to me. Listen to me, and your soul will live. I will establish an everlasting covenant with you, the faithful kindness promised to David.
Look, I have made you a witness to the peoples, a ruler and leader of the nations.
You will call nations you did not know, and nations that do not know you will run to you, because of the Lord your God and because of the Holy One of Israel, who has glorified you.
Seek the Lord, and when you find him, call on him when he is near.
Let the sinner abandon his way and the wicked man his thoughts. Let him return to me, and I will have mercy on him, and to our God, who forgives abundantly.
For my thoughts are not like your thoughts, and my ways are not like your ways, says the Lord.
For just as the heavens are higher than the earth, so my ways are higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For just as rain and snow come down from heaven and do not return there, but water the earth, make it produce and sprout, and give seed to the sower and bread to eat,
So shall my word be that goes out from my mouth: it will not return to me empty, but will do what I desire and accomplish what I sent it to do.
For you will go out with joy and depart in peace. The mountains and hills will rejoice before you with praise, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
Instead of the thornbush, the cypress will grow, and instead of the nettle, the myrtle will grow. This will bring renown to the Lord and be an everlasting sign that will never end.
Thus says the Lord: Maintain justice and practice righteousness, for my salvation is near to coming and my righteousness to being revealed.
Blessed is the person who does this, the human being who holds firmly to it, who also keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hands from doing evil.
Let no foreigner who joins himself to the Lord say, “The Lord will certainly separate me from his people.” And let no eunuch say, “I am a dry tree.”
For thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, choose what I desire, and hold firmly to my covenant:
I will give them a place and a name in my house and within my walls, better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will never end.

And as for the foreigners who join themselves to the Lord to serve him, to love the name of the Lord, and to be his servants—all who also keep the Sabbath without profaning it and hold firmly to my covenant—

I will bring them to my holy mountain and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be acceptable on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
This is what the Lord God says, who gathers the scattered people of Israel: I will gather still others to him, in addition to those already gathered.
Every wild animal of the field, come and devour all the animals of the forest!
The seers are all blind and know nothing. They are all mute dogs, unable to bark. They dream and lie asleep, and they love to slumber.
They are dogs with greedy appetites, never knowing satisfaction. They will be wicked and have no understanding. They have all turned to their own way, each to his own side and his own direction.
Come, let us get wine and get strong drink, and let it be as it is today, with a great deal more left over for us.
Look, the righteous person perishes, and no one takes it to heart. Godly people are taken away, with no one understanding, for the righteous person is taken away from evil.
Peace will come, and they will rest on their beds and go straight ahead.
But you, come here, children of [?], adulterous and promiscuous offspring!
Whom have you mocked? Against whom have you opened your mouths and stretched out your tongues? Look, you are children of injustice and offspring of falsehood,
who take comfort in idols under every leafy tree and have slaughtered children in the valleys beneath rocky cliffs.
Your portion and your inheritance are with the portion of the valleys. Upon them you have also poured out drink offerings and presented offerings. Shall I be comforted by these things?
On high and lofty mountains you made your bed, and you also went up there to offer sacrifices.

Behind the doors, on the doorposts, you have inscribed your memorial. For you uncovered yourself away from me, went up, and enlarged your bed. You made yourself one of them, loved their bed, and saw a place.
You made yourself splendid for kings with oil and multiplied your perfumes. You sent your messengers far away and humbled yourself as far as Sheol.
You grew weary from your many journeys, yet you did not say, “I will stop.” In the guilt of your hands you [?]; therefore you did not plead for mercy.
Of whom were you so terrified and afraid that you lied to me, did not remember me, and did not consider me in your heart? Look, I am the Holy One from eternity, yet you did not fear me.
I will reveal my righteousness, and your deeds will not benefit you.

When you cry out, let those who gather to you rescue you. The wind will carry them all away, and a whirlwind will take them. But those who hope in me will inherit the land and inherit my holy mountain.
They will say, ‘Clear it, clear it! Prepare the road! Remove the stumbling blocks from the road of my people!’

For thus says the high and exalted one, who dwells forever and whose name is holy: His dwelling is high and holy, and is for the humble and those distressed in spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble and revive the heart of the suffering.
For I will not contend forever, nor will I remain angry forever, because the spirit goes out from me, and I made the breath of life.
Because of the wickedness of her deceit, I was angry and struck her. I turned away and was angry, but she went on wantonly in the way of her heart.
I have seen her ways and healed her. I have comforted her and restored comfort to her and to her mourners.
I create the speech of lips: ‘Peace, peace to those far away and those nearby,’ says the Lord, ‘and I will heal them.’
The wicked are troubled like the sea, because they cannot be still, and its waters toss up debris and mud.
‘There is no peace for the wicked,’ says my God.
Cry out at the top of your voice; do not hold back. Raise your voice like a trumpet. Declare to my people their wrongdoing and to the house of Jacob their sins.

They seek me every day and desire to know my ways, like a people who practiced righteousness and did not abandon the justice of their God. They ask me for justice and righteousness and desire to draw near to God.
Why have we fasted, and you have not seen? Why have we humbled ourselves, and you have not noticed? Look, on the day of your fast you do as you please and bring forward all your idols.
Look, you fast for quarrelling and fighting, and to strike with wicked violence. Do not fast as you do today, expecting to make your voice heard on high.
Is this the fast I have chosen: for someone to humble himself, bend his neck like a reed, and spread sackcloth and ashes beneath himself? Will you call this a fast and a day pleasing to the Lord?
This is the fast I have chosen: to loosen the bonds of wickedness, cut the restraints of deceit, and set the oppressed free. You must break every bond.
Share your bread with the hungry, and bring the stranger into your house. When you see someone naked, clothe him, and do not neglect your own flesh and blood.
Then your light will break forth like the morning, and your righteousness will quickly dawn. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the Lord will gather you in.
Then you will call, and the Lord will answer you. You will cry out, and he will say, “Here I am,” if you remove deceit from among you, release the oppressed, and keep away from false speech.
If you give your bread to the hungry and satisfy the hungry person, your light will rise in the darkness, and your darkness will be like midday.
The Lord will guide you continually, satisfy you with rich food, and strengthen your bones. You will be like a flourishing garden and like a spring whose waters never fail.

Your descendants will rebuild the ancient ruins, and you will raise up foundations that have lain for generations. You will be called the repairer of breaches and the restorer of paths for people to live along.

If you turn your foot away from the Sabbath, so that you do not do as you please on my holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight and the Lord’s holy day honorable, and honor it by not going your own way on it, not doing as you please on it, and not speaking a word,
then you will trust in the Lord, who will make you ride over the strongholds of the earth and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.
Look, the Lord’s hand is not too short to save, nor is his ear too dull to hear.
But your offenses have separated you from your God, and your sins have turned his face away from you so that he does not hear.
For your hands are stained with blood and your fingers with wickedness. Your lips speak lies, and your tongue devises injustice.
No one pleads a case righteously, and no one judges faithfully. They trust in emptiness and speak worthless things. They conceive wickedness and give birth to suffering.
They hatch vipers’ eggs and weave a spider’s web. Whoever eats their eggs will die, and whoever breaks one finds a venomous snake.
Their web will not serve as clothing, and they will not cover themselves with what they make. Their deeds are deeds of wickedness, and acts of injustice are in their hands.
Their feet run toward evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are thoughts of wickedness, and plunder and destruction are in their paths.
They have not known the way of peace, and there is no justice in their ways. Their paths are crooked, and whoever walks in them does not know peace.
Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We waited for light, but there was darkness; for brightness, but we walked in gloom.
We grope along the wall like the blind, and grope like those who have no eyes. We stumble at noon as though it were evening, and sigh like those who are near death.
We all growl like bears and moan like doves. We wait for justice, but there is none, and for salvation, but it is far from us.
For our wickedness is great before you, and our sins bear witness. Our wickedness is with us, and our sins are known.
We have acted wickedly and dealt falsely with the Lord, and turned away from following our God. We have spoken oppression and rebelled; we have conceived and devised lying words in our hearts.
We have turned justice backward and kept righteousness at a distance, for truth has stumbled in the streets, and correction cannot enter.
